# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Differentiate the background of the In Review header

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, all group section headers (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ▼ ──`, `── Idea (2) ──`, `── In Review (5) ──`) are rendered identically — bold, with a foreground stage colour and no background fill. The producer cannot distinguish the In Review section from other sections at a glance, which matters because In Review items are the only ones with an active producer-review obligation. Give the In Review header a grey background so the section stands out visually.

## Users

- **Herdr users (primarily the producer / session operator)** who scan the selection list for the In Review queue and need to locate that section quickly.
  - User story: "As a Herdr user reviewing the selection list, I want the In Review header to have a distinctive grey background so I can spot the review queue section immediately, even when the list is long."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour, e.g. `ANSI.bg(238)` or a nearby grey value) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other group heading rows (e.g. `Group N`, `Idea`, `Completed`, etc.) are unchanged — no background fill added.
- AC3: The selected-heading highlight still works: when the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing reverse-video selection bar (`reverseWrap`) remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, count, collapse arrow, and width-truncation behaviour are unaffected by the background change (single-row heading invariant preserved).
- AC5: Unit tests cover the new rendering: a heading with label `In Review` contains the background escape sequence, and other headings do not; existing heading-render tests still pass.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Use existing ANSI helpers in `worklist.ts` (`ANSI.bg(code)` with a 256-colour code) — no new dependencies.
- Must not change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Implementation must be keyed off the heading's `groupLabel === 'In Review'` (the label originates in `grouping.ts`); keep the label source as the single source of truth.

## Existing state

- Group heading rows are first-class rows in the display-rows model (`DisplayHeadingRow`), interleaved by `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- The heading row is rendered in `createListRenderer` at `worklist.ts:~4482`:
  `const line = `${indent} ${ANSI.fg(stageColor(undefined))}${ANSI.bold}── ${row.groupLabel} (${row.count}) ${arrow} ──${ANSI.reset}``
- `ANSI.bg(code)` exists at `worklist.ts:~345` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`) and is already used for banner fills (e.g. `ANSI.bg(196)`, `ANSI.bg(220)`, `ANSI.bg(40)`).
- The `In Review` group label is assigned in `grouping.ts:~309` (`groupLabel: 'In Review'` for `stage === 'in_review'`).
- Selected rows are wrapped with `reverseWrap` (re-asserts `\x1b[0m` resets to keep the whole selected row highlighted); heading rows have no interior resets so they are handled fine.

## Desired change

- In the heading-row render branch of `createListRenderer`, when `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, wrap the line's base style with a grey background (`${ANSI.bg(238)}` or similar), keeping the existing foreground/bold styling and the existing `reverseWrap` interaction on selection. Other headings render as today.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch (`createListRenderer`, ~line 4482); add conditional grey background for `groupLabel === 'In Review'`; `ANSI.bg` helper at ~line 345.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — extend with tests asserting the background escape sequence on `In Review` headings and its absence on others.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `stageColor`/ANSI conventions (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- Grey background may reduce contrast against the 220 (yellow-ish) foreground `stageColor` for in-review headings; mitigate by choosing a dark grey (238) and verifying readability. If contrast is insufficient, the foreground can be switched to white (231) for this heading only — record the choice in the implementation.
- Selection visibility: reverse-wrap must stay visible over the background — covered by AC3; verify selection rendering in a terminal, not just by string matching.
- Scope creep: do NOT extend the background to other headings unless separately requested — that is a separate work item (recorded here to avoid accidental bundling).
- Test brittleness: assert on the presence of the `\x1b[48;5;...m` background sequence for the In Review heading rather than on exact full-row strings, to avoid coupling to foreground/bold detail changes.

## Related work

- **Duplicate check performed** — no overlapping completed item found. Related completed items (none duplicates): WL-0MS4FIEN40037GB9 (total actionable count in Herdr header), WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB (in_progress/in_review in mandatory In Review set), WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ (selection-list refresh on tab focus), WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 (heading rows as first-class display rows — this feature builds on that model).
- `docs/icons-design.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed description ("make the In Review header background gray (or similar) to differentiate that section from other sections") was specific enough to draft the brief directly. Assumption recorded: "gray (or similar)" means a grey ANSI 256 background (default candidate: 238, same value already used elsewhere in `worklist.ts`), applied only to the In Review heading; other section headers remain unchanged. Rationale: description explicitly scopes differentiation to "that section".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKW1GUSC1DSWYGS** – OpenCode (completed)
- **WL-0ML1LBF6H0NE40RX** – Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes (completed)
- **WL-0ML4DOK1U19NN8LG** – Add wl list --parent <id> for child-only listing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection, similar
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection

# Grey background on In Review heading

## Summary

In `createListRenderer`'s heading-row branch, give the heading whose `groupLabel === 'In Review'` a grey ANSI 256 background fill while leaving every other heading unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour via the existing `ANSI.bg(code)` helper, default `ANSI.bg(238)`) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other heading rows (`Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `Completed`, etc.) render exactly as before — no background escape added.
- AC3: When the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing `reverseWrap(line)` selection bar remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, item count, collapse arrow (`▼`/`▶`), depth indentation, and width truncation are unchanged; the single-row heading invariant and line-count accounting are preserved.
- AC5: The grey choice keeps the heading legible; if contrast against the existing foreground is insufficient, switch this heading's foreground to white (`ANSI.fg(231)`) and record the choice in a code comment.
- AC6: The full project test suite passes with the change (run via the project test skill).
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (on the heading-render branch) and the relevant section of `packages/herdr/README.md` (and any relevant wiki or docs site entries).

## Constraints

- Use the existing `ANSI.bg(code)` helper in `worklist.ts` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`, ~line 357) — no new dependencies.
- Do NOT change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Key the condition off `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, keeping the label source (`grouping.ts` ~line 309) as the single source of truth.
- Do NOT extend the background to other headings — that is out of scope.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch in `createListRenderer` (~line 4482) and the `ANSI.bg` helper (~line 357).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions to update for AC7.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `const bg = row.groupLabel === 'In Review' ? ANSI.bg(238) : '';` in the heading branch and prepend it to the line's base style (keep foreground + bold + trailing `ANSI.reset`).

## Deliverables

- Updated `worklist.ts` heading render branch implementing AC1–AC5; doc/comment updates (AC7); suite green (AC6). Resolution of the grey/contrast choice recorded in a code comment (AC5).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Test: In Review heading background rendering` (test-first ordering, parent AC5); dependency edge wired.

# Remove fast/cheap mode switches, replace with priority on requests

## Problem statement

The LLM proxy has retired its global fast/cheap operating mode in favour of a
per-request priority header (`X-Priority: low|medium|high`, default `medium`),
implemented and verified on `llm-manager` `dev` (commit `e5d3a2bf`,
LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA). Herdr still carries the client half of the retired
design: an activity-gated mode-switch worker that POSTs `/admin/set-mode`, a
scheduler task and three settings keys that exist only to drive it, and
mode-keyed audit Phase-2 parallelism. Because herdr sends no priority, it can
no longer express urgency or cost intent now that the proxy has no mode to
switch.

## Users

- **Agent operator (producer/developer)** running the herdr worklist — wants
  interactive dispatches served responsively without flipping a global mode,
  and unattended downtime work served cheaply and politely.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — wants each dispatched item's priority to reach the
  proxy so high/critical work outranks background work.
- **Pi agent panes launched by herdr** — must convey the scheduled work item's
  priority on every provider request without user action.

### Example user stories

- As a herdr user, when I dispatch a `high`-priority item interactively, its
  LLM requests carry `X-Priority: high` so they skip the contention queue and
  may fall back to remote immediately.
- As the downtime dispatcher, a `low`-priority item is dispatched with
  `X-Priority: low` so it prefers a queued local slot over paid remote work,
  while a `critical` item is dispatched with `X-Priority: high`.
- As a maintainer, the herdr plugin no longer contains or configures a
  mode-switch worker, and removing `modeSwitch*` keys from my settings file is
  optional (old files keep loading).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mode-switching client machinery is removed.** `mode-switch-worker.ts` and
   its tests, the `mode-switch` scheduler task, the
   `modeSwitchEnabled`/`modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`/`modeSwitchPollIntervalMs`
   settings (types, defaults, parsing, validation), the `onOperatorCommand`
   hook, the `onProxyIdle` callback, and every `/admin/set-mode` call are gone.
   No shipped code or operational doc references fast/cheap mode switching;
   the plugin starts and dispatches normally.
2. **Interactive dispatch priority mapping** is implemented and unit-tested:
   work-item `low` → request `medium`, `medium` → `high`, `high` → `high`,
   `critical` → `high`; no resolvable work item (free-form `/prompt:`,
   lookup failure) → `high`.
3. **Downtime dispatch priority mapping** is implemented and unit-tested:
   work-item `low` → `low`, `medium` → `medium`, `high` → `high`,
   `critical` → `high`; unknown priority → `medium`.
4. **The Pi Worklog extension injects `X-Priority` on every provider request.**
   It reads the pane-launch env `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, accepts only
   `low|medium|high`, and sets the header via `before_provider_headers`.
   Unset or invalid values leave headers untouched (the proxy then applies its
   own `medium` default). Unit tests cover valid, invalid and unset values.
5. **Mode-keyed audit Phase-2 parallelism is removed.** `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`
   is always `1` (fully serial, per producer decision); the
   `DowntimeSpawnConfig`/`mode`/`slotBudget` plumbing is deleted while the
   existing free-slot gating is unchanged.
6. **Testing criterion:** new/updated unit tests cover the two mapping
   functions, settings config-passthrough/backward compatibility, the
   extension header injection, and the dispatcher/pane spawn environment.
7. **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`,
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` and `LOCAL_LLM.md`;
   `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` is removed.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No changes to `llm-manager`.** The wire contract is fixed by the proxy
  implementation: request header `X-Priority` with values
  `low|medium|high`, absent → `medium`; the proxy applies its own cheap-window
  effective-priority cap and reports `X-Priority-Applied` for observability.
- Header injection must be **fail-open**: a missing/invalid
  `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` results in no header, never an assumed `high`.
- The priority is conveyed as a **pane-launch environment variable**
  (`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`), consumed by the globally installed Worklog pi
  extension, so it works for every pi session herdr launches (interactive
  pane, headless background run, downtime pane).
- **Backward compatibility:** existing herdr settings files containing the
  retired keys must keep loading (unknown keys ignored, no migration needed).
- Work lands on `dev` only, via the standard worktree/implement flow.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` (~550 lines) implements
  activity-gated fast/cheap switching: `getAdminMode`/`setProxyMode` over
  `/admin/set-mode`, a shared activity file, leader-only idle switching, a
  model-cooldown gate, and an operator-command fast switch.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` defines `modeSwitchEnabled`,
  `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`, `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` (defaults, clamping,
  parse).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` constructs the worker, wires `onProxyIdle`,
  calls `onOperatorCommand` on agent-route dispatch, and passes the observed
  mode into the downtime dispatcher.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` registers the `mode-switch` scheduler task
  and accepts the worker/poll-interval options.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` derives
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` from `DowntimeSpawnConfig` (`mode`, `slotBudget`,
  `freeSlots`, `concurrentDispatchCap`).
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` splits a pane (`grid.py`) and runs
  `run-pi-agent.sh` via `herdr pane run`; `run-in-pane.sh` splits and runs
  shell commands. Neither passes request-priority information.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` registers agent-side pi modules
  (activity indicator, model display, session health, guardrails, recovery,
  lease release); it has no provider-header hook.
- The proxy side is live: `proxy/proxy/priority.py` in `llm-manager` parses
  `X-Priority`, computes an effective priority, and routes per request.

## Desired change

1. Delete the mode-switch worker, its tests, the scheduler task, the settings
   keys and all wiring; strip mode-aware Phase-2 parallelism (serial Phase 2).
2. Add explicit request-priority mapping helpers: interactive
   (`low→medium`, `medium/high/critical→high`, default `high`) and downtime
   (`low/medium/high→same`, `critical→high`, unknown→`medium`).
3. Thread the mapped priority into every agent dispatch. Herdr resolves the
   dispatched item's work-item priority at dispatch time (from the worklist
   item cache or a fail-open `wl show` lookup) and maps it per the table
   above:
   - interactive agent panes and headless `spawnBackgroundPi` runs set
     `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` in the child env and pass it through
     `send-to-pi.sh` to the pane process (e.g. `exec env HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=… bash run-pi-agent.sh …`,
     or `herdr pane split --env`/`grid.py` passthrough in resize mode);
   - downtime panes set the same env in `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` from the
     selected `DowntimeCandidate.priority`.
4. Add a Worklog pi extension module that validates
   `process.env.HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` and sets the `X-Priority` request
   header via `before_provider_headers`, leaving headers untouched otherwise.
5. Update/remove docs and tests as described in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — delete (worker, idle
  detection, set-mode client, activity file, cooldown gate).
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts` — delete.
- `packages/herdr/src/drain-regression-guard.test.ts` — delete or repurpose;
  it exists solely to guard the removed cheap-switch path.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — remove the three `modeSwitch*` keys,
  their defaults, clamping/parse logic and the import from the deleted module.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` — drop mode-switch cases; add a
  backward-compatibility case proving retired keys are ignored.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — remove worker construction/holder,
  `onProxyIdle`, `onOperatorCommand`, and the `mode` passed to the downtime
  dispatcher; add request-priority resolution for interactive dispatch and
  pass `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` to pane/headless spawns.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — remove the mode-switch scheduler task,
  worker/poll-interval options and related imports.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — remove `DowntimeSpawnConfig`
  mode/slot-budget plumbing, set `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '1'`, add the
  downtime priority mapping and env var to `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — accept/forward the request-priority
  env var into the spawned pane process; update usage docs.
- `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — forward the env var through the
  `pane.split` RPC when the resize path is used (fallback: pass it in the
  `pane run` command).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — if shell panes are given priority
  context, mirror the passthrough (otherwise document the exclusion).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.ts` — new: validate
  `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, map to the header; register
  `before_provider_headers`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts` — new tests.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` — register the module.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `CONFIG.md`, `LOCAL_LLM.md` — remove mode-switch/settings documentation and
  document the priority mapping and env var.
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` — delete.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** (`llm-manager`, completed/in_review) — proxy-side
  priority routing replacing fast/cheap mode (`X-Priority` header, effective
  priority window, per-model `priority_routes`). This item is the client half.
- **LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR** (`llm-manager`) — trust-gate hardening for the
  priority header (`high` currently claimable by any reachable client).
  Related, **not** blocking: herdr is an internal client.
- **WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME** — mode-aware audit Phase-2 parallelism (the feature
  being removed here).
- **WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9**, **WL-0MV563AU2007FM56**, **WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ**,
  **WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR**, **WL-0MUL0KO7Q003O7YJ** — model-cooldown /
  drain / cheap-switch history. The `model-cooldown` signal itself stays (it
  is also read by `stalled-work.ts`); only the cheap-switch gate consumer is
  removed.
- **WL-0MU5BOK3P0090O0V** — proxy mode flapping RCA (one of the failure modes
  the removal eliminates).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRE6JDT3004OSTF** – proactively release leases (completed)
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T** – Investigate poller identity on proxy:8000 — attribute each status_request poller (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mt50s9jw001dhme, 0muwihul2000jefr, 0mv5638zs005i5xq, absent, accept (+399 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0muwihul2000jefr, 0mv54zp3y00514y9, absent, accept, accepted (+346 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, accept, accepted, accepts, action (+290 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — dispatch regression in the resize path.** The resize split is
  performed by `grid.py` over a JSON-RPC socket; if the socket payload does not
  accept `env`, the priority must be injected in the `pane run` command
  instead. Mitigation: unit-test the script argument builder and verify one
  real pane launch; keep the header path fail-open so a missing env never
  blocks a request.
- **Risk — throughput loss.** Forcing `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` makes audit
  Phase 2 fully serial (producer decision Q2b). Accepted: it avoids inventing
  a replacement mode concept and never overfills the 2-slot pool.
- **Risk — stale user settings.** Retired keys in existing settings files must
  be ignored, not rejected. Mitigation: explicit backward-compatibility test.
- **Risk — priority is per session, not per request.** A pane launched for one
  item that later works another item keeps the original priority. Accepted for
  v1; mid-session re-prioritisation is out of scope.
- **Scope-creep guard:** proxy-side trust-gate hardening (LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR)
  and any proxy code change are out of scope; any opportunity discovered during
  implementation is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.
- **Assumption:** shell-command panes (`!!`/`!`) do not need priority context
  because they do not schedule agent work; only agent dispatch paths
  (interactive pane, headless agent run, downtime pane) set it.
- **Assumption:** interactive priority resolution is fail-open — if the item
  cannot be resolved (no ID, `wl show` failure, timeout) the dispatch still
  proceeds with the interactive default `high`.
- **Assumption:** the installed herdr binary supports `pane split --env`
  (verified on the current host, herdr 0.7.5 CLI help); if not, the
  `exec env …` launch form is the fallback.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should herdr convey per-request priority when the proxy side was
  not yet visible in `llm-manager` dev?**
  - Options: (a) agree the contract now and record the proxy dependency;
    (b) block until the proxy lands; (c) make header name/mapping configurable.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "I believe the proxy side is now
    implemented. Please git pull on ../llm-manager and verify."
  - **Research:** `git pull` fast-forwarded to `24348bfa`; commit `e5d3a2bf`
    ("priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode (X-Priority header +
    per-model priority tiers)") adds `proxy/proxy/priority.py`:
    `X-Priority: low|medium|high`, default `medium`, effective-priority
    cheap-window cap, `X-Priority-Applied` response header. Work item
    **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** is `completed`/`in_review`. Contract adopted: (a),
    with the fixed header name `X-Priority` and no configurability.
- **Q2: What happens to mode-aware logic (`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`,
  `spawnConfig.mode`/`slotBudget`)?**
  - Options: (a) derive from free slots + slot budget; (b) fix parallelism to
    `1` (fully serial); (c) keep a constant pseudo-mode.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "b".
  - **Decision:** remove the mode plumbing; `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is
    always `'1'`; free-slot gating unchanged.
- **Q3: Default priority for interactive requests with no resolvable work
  item (free-form `/prompt:`, shell panes, missing ID)?**
  - Options: (a) `high`; (b) `medium`; (c) no header (proxy default).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "a".
  - **Decision:** default interactive request priority is `high`.

# Intake Brief: Herdr audit dispatch — deepen per-window batch when the in_review queue is deep (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS)

## Headline

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher drain a deep `completed`/`in_review` backlog faster by allowing **sequential** audit dispatches to continue within one continuous idle window (up to a small cap) whenever the audit-eligible queue depth reaches `browseItemCount`. Concurrency safety is unchanged: at most one audit is ever active, and every dispatch still passes the idle-duration gate, the ≥2 free-slot minimum, the host-wide audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher currently requires a fresh full idle period after **every** successful dispatch (`tracker.record(false)` in the worker tick), and the host-wide active-audit marker (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) blocks a second audit dispatch while one is running. Under sustained agent traffic, idle windows are rare, so the audit tier drains at roughly one item per idle window even when the `completed`/`in_review` queue is dozens of items deep. The audit skill can already process several items per seeded run (batch drain, SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5), but herdr only ever seeds a single-item `/skill:audit <id>` dispatch.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — wants the review queue to drain during idle compute so items reach release sooner.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deeper than my sprint window, I want the dispatcher to use one idle window for several audits (one after another) instead of one audit per window, so the backlog drains days faster without any extra LLM load.
- **Downtime dispatcher operator** — wants predictable, observable batching that never breaks the safety gates or the host-wide audit slot.
  - *User story:* As an operator, when the queue is shallow I want exactly today's behaviour, and when batching is active I want to see why each extra audit was (or was not) dispatched in the decision log.
- **Audit-tier agents** — must keep receiving one work item per dispatch and never see a duplicate or concurrent audit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Depth-aware batching: an audit-eligible depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` above 1 allows distinct audit continuations inside one idle window until the cap or the depth drop.

  Details: **Depth-aware audit batching (opt-in by depth).** When the audit-eligible backlog — root `completed`/`in_review` items that `classifyItemForDispatch` maps to `audit` (i.e. without a fresh audit and not held) — is at least `browseItemCount`, and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2, clamped, `1` = legacy/off) is greater than 1, the dispatcher may continue dispatching distinct audit targets within the same continuous idle window until the cap is reached or the depth drops below the threshold. When the depth is below the threshold, behaviour is unchanged: one dispatch per window and a fresh idle period is required before the next.

- Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.

  Details: **Sequential single-audit safety.** The batch continuation never starts a second audit while one is active: it waits for the previous audit's host-wide/per-worklog marker to be released, and re-checks — on every continuation — the continuous idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention (`contention_queue_depth == 0`), the code-freeze marker, the machine-wide active-audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight. No gate is relaxed or bypassed; only the post-dispatch "require a fresh full idle period" reset is deferred for an audit-batch continuation.

- No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.

  Details: **No duplicate or re-dispatched items.** Each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware marker release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A failed CAS claim, claim rollback, spawn failure, or any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the current batch rather than skipping to another target.

- Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

  Details: **Coordination-mode compatibility.** On the production coordination path the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking path) without releasing leadership mid-batch; leadership hand-off still occurs once after the batch ends when the fallback was used. When the depth drops below threshold or the cap is reached, normal single-dispatch behaviour resumes immediately.

- Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

  Details: **Observability.** Every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`, and the existing tokens for held/blocked continuations), including depth, cap and remaining count. Existing reason tokens and rate limiting are unchanged.

- Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.

  Details: **Test coverage (herdr package).** Unit tests assert: (a) shallow depth keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour including the idle-tracker reset; (b) depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window; (c) an unsatisfied idle-duration gate (and sub-2 free slots) blocks all dispatch, including continuations; (d) the host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation, and continuation proceeds only after release; (e) the cap and the depth-drop are respected; (f) dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice.

- Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

  Details: **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

  Details: **Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (at minimum the full herdr package suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the strict idle-duration gate and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` for every dispatch: reserve at least one local slot, and never fan out concurrent audits.
- The host-wide single-audit contract (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) remains the hard concurrency cap; this item changes only *cadence within one idle window*, never audit concurrency.
- Must not destabilise leader election/lease (5-minute TTL), coordination check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups, the review-queue gate, or the coordination offer path.
- Reuse `browseItemCount` (`readReviewQueueGate` / `resolveSprintViewWindow`) as the single "deep queue" threshold; do not add a second depth definition.
- The new setting is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (settings key `downtimeAuditBatchMax`), default `2`, clamped to a safe range; `1` disables batching and restores legacy behaviour.
- No SorraAgents/audit-skill changes: the audit skill's own batch drain remains the mechanism that processes multiple items after a dispatch; herdr only decides how many audit panes to seed per window.
- Do not change the legacy `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier chain's semantics beyond the shared continuation logic; the production path is coordination mode.
- **Out of scope:** relaxing the host-wide single-audit marker, changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS`/`AUDIT_BATCH_TIMEOUT` in SorraAgents, and any non-audit batching.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` consumes the Herdr list head and applies safety gates as sequential filters; `dispatchFromCoordination` (leader) dispatches at most one offer per tick and only reads its own extended head as a fallback when nothing in the offer list is dispatchable; the worker `tick()` calls `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])` after a successful dispatch, which is the per-window reset.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `readReviewQueueGate` already measures the root-only `completed`/`in_review` count against `browseItemCount` (`resolveSprintViewWindow`), and `classifyItemForDispatch` already decides whether an item is an audit candidate, including freshness/recency.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `getActiveAudit` checks the machine-wide `~/.herdr/downtime/active-audit` marker before the per-worklog dispatch-log marker; `recordDispatch` writes both, `recordPaneClose`/`recordDispatchFailure` release them.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` wires the Herdr head, `fetchItem`, `getActiveAudit`, dispatch markers and the pane-close hooks.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — downtime settings plumbing, defaults and clamping (the new `downtimeAuditBatchMax` follows the same pattern).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — where the existing single-dispatch and audit-tier behaviour is asserted.

## Desired change

1. Add a bounded, depth-derived batch mode: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head (root `completed`/`in_review` items are mandatory in the head), activate only when `depth >= browseItemCount` and `downtimeAuditBatchMax > 1`, and expose the remaining budget to the dispatch path.
2. In `tick()`, replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one: on a successful **audit** dispatch in active batch mode with budget remaining, keep the idle tracker armed for an audit continuation (subject to a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check); for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, preserve today's reset exactly.
3. In `dispatchFromCoordination`, allow the leader to source a continuation audit target from its own head extension after a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion; defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.
4. Add `downtimeAuditBatchMax` to settings (default 2, clamped, 1 = off) and thread it through `DowntimeWorkerConfig` and the dispatch options.
5. Record `audit-batch-continue` (and held variants) in the decision log, with depth/cap/remaining metadata, at the existing rate limit.
6. Add the unit tests listed in AC6 and update the dispatcher docs/README.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — batch depth computation, continuation budget, conditional idle reset, leader continuation path, decision-log token.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeAuditBatchMax` default, parsing and clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — thread the new setting into `createDowntimeWorker`/dispatch config.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — depth-aware batch activation, cap and marker/single-flight safety tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — shallow-depth regression and idle-reset behaviour.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` — worker-loop continuation, idle gate blocking, leadership hand-off timing.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — leader own-head continuation and distinct-target guarantees.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — setting default/clamp coverage.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — activation rule, sequential safety invariants, decision tokens.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — operator-facing description of the new setting.

## Related work

- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV — active-audit single-flight (per-worklog); preserved per item, not relaxed.
- WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA — host-wide audit serialisation; remains the hard concurrency cap.
- WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 — per-tier free-slot minimums (audit needs 2); reused unchanged.
- WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — downtime dispatcher leader election and coordination.
- WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 — own-backlog fallback relinquishes leadership; must be deferred to batch end.
- WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 — sprint-view-only dispatch window (`browseItemCount` head).
- WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB — active-audit detection and audit-tier skip (per-worklog marker).
- WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9 — review-queue depth gate (same `browseItemCount` signal).
- WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD — review-queue gate rewiring (neutral `review-queue-hold`).
- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (SorraAgents) — audit batch drain that consumes the seeded window.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: non-audit tiers could be starved** while a batch continues. Mitigation: batching applies only to audit dispatches and only while `depth >= browseItemCount`; as soon as no audit candidate remains, the normal tier/ranking resumes.
- **Risk: leadership hand-off logic regressed.** The existing own-backlog dispatch releases leadership immediately; deferring it for a batch could strand the leader if the batch never ends. Mitigation: release at batch end, on any failed continuation, and on the next tick when the cap/depth condition no longer holds; cover with an orchestrator test.
- **Risk: the idle-reset change leaks into other kinds.** Mitigation: scope the conditional reset to the audit-batch continuation flag only; add a regression test asserting non-audit dispatch still resets the tracker.
- **Risk: extra `wl` reads per tick hurt latency.** Mitigation: derive depth from the already-fetched head; no new subprocess in the common path.
- **Risk: a continuation starts during a code freeze or after the queue drops.** Mitigation: re-read the freeze marker and re-compute depth on every continuation tick; any frozen/ambiguous state or depth < threshold simply ends the batch and restores normal behaviour.
- **Assumption:** `completed`/`in_review` root items are mandatory-always in the Herdr head, so the head is a complete depth source up to `browseItemCount` and beyond (the existing window extension covers overflow).
- **Assumption:** the host-wide marker is released when the audit pane closes (`recordPaneClose`) or a spawn fails, so a continuation can start promptly without weakening the marker's stale window.
- **Assumption:** a sequential audit batch is acceptable to the audit runner's host-wide `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` slot because at most one audit pane is active at a time.
- **Scope-creep risk:** relaxing host-wide serialisation (option B) or changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` (option C) is explicitly out of scope; if either becomes necessary it should be raised as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mechanism):** How should "more than one audit per window" work — (A) keep exactly one active audit and continue sequentially within a continuous idle window, (B) dispatch N audit panes in one tick, or (C) seed the audit skill's batch queue with N ids?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** — keep exactly one active audit; when depth ≥ threshold, skip the fresh-idle-period reset so the next audit dispatches once the previous audit pane closes and slots are idle again.
  - **Evidence:** host-wide active-audit marker semantics (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` § Host-wide audit serialisation) and `tick()`'s post-dispatch `tracker.record(false)`.
- **Q2 (threshold):** Reuse `browseItemCount` or add a dedicated threshold?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **Reuse `browseItemCount`** as the single deep-queue signal; add only the small cap `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2).
  - **Evidence:** `readReviewQueueGate`/`resolveSprintViewWindow` already define "deep" for the review-queue gate.
- **Q3 (second target source):** Where should the extra audit target(s) come from in coordination mode?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** the leader re-reads its own Herdr head after the first dispatch (extend the existing own-backlog fallback).
  - **Evidence:** `dispatchFromCoordination`'s own-backlog fallback (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`) and WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7** – RCA: no downtime dispatch overnight despite continuous idle-window status polling (~16 polls/min, 7h idle) (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** – Check dispatch logs/leases on 192.168.0.191 filesystem (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4VB009HIJL** – Tests: getChordByPrefix and arbitrary-depth dispatch (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, 0mt3phw4i002snov, 60s, ac1 (+120 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt3phw4i002snov, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+110 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, 60s, ac1, ac3 (+83 more)

# Decompose the `downtime-worker.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (8,105 lines, 174 exported symbols, 23 logical sections)

## Problem statement

`downtime-worker.ts` has grown into a single 8,105-line module that carries the
entire downtime-dispatch subsystem: constants, public types, idle detection,
the local-status poller, dispatchability gates, the Herdr list-head dispatch
pipeline, leader-election coordination, pane spawning and lifecycle, the worker
tick orchestrator, wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, settings clamps and
round-robin helpers. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one concern
requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch change carries
avoidable regression risk.

## Users

- **Downtime-dispatch maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one
  concern (e.g. a gate, a tier parser, the spawn path) without reasoning about
  8,000 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need to review a focused diff where the blast radius of
  a change is legible from the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing dispatch work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a dispatch-gate change, I want the gate logic in a
  dedicated module so that I can modify it without re-reading the whole worker.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff to be attributable to a single concern so
  that I can verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so that the file is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./downtime-worker.js` by another module remains exported from
   that exact path with identical types and values, so the 33 importing files
   compile with no import-path edits. The barrel re-exports **only symbols that
   are actually used** by consumers; symbols that nothing outside the split
   modules imports are internal and need not be re-exported (producer decision
   on Q2).
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `downtime-worker.js` barrel; the dependency
   check reports no new cycles and does not extend the pre-existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle into runtime values.
5. **Single-flight state remains singular.** The module-level mutable
   `dispatchInFlightCount` (current line 2523) lives in exactly one module and
   is not duplicated by the split, so per-process dispatch single-flight
   semantics are unchanged.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and the existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic,
  rename public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 33 files import from `./downtime-worker.js`,
  including 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites (~15,000 test lines) and the
  production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts`, plus 11 other test files.
  The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, clamps/parsers) and work inwards, so each merged step leaves the build
  and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or dispatch behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** The item targets `downtime-worker.ts`; the other
  `packages/herdr` files above 1,000 lines are explicitly out of scope (see
  Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`downtime-worker.ts` is 8,105 lines. Its section inventory (line ranges from the
current `dev` checkout) is:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Constants | 204–616 | 413 |
| 2 | Types | 617–709 | 93 |
| 3 | Idle detection | 710–862 | 153 |
| 4 | Idle-duration tracker | 863–902 | 40 |
| 5 | Per-slot idle tracker | 903–964 | 62 |
| 6 | Poller | 965–1248 | 284 |
| 7 | Dispatch (types + claim/result helpers) | 1249–2538 | 1,290 |
| 8 | Review-queue depth gate | 2539–2724 | 186 |
| 9 | Critical-only dispatch-window escape hatch | 2725–2776 | 52 |
| 10 | Herdr list-head filter dispatcher | 2777–3695 | 919 |
| 11 | Leader-election coordination dispatch | 3696–5614 | 1,919 |
| 12 | Pane-lifecycle monitor | 5615–5773 | 159 |
| 13 | Worker orchestrator | 5774–6932 | 1,159 |
| 14 | Blocked-questions prompt | 6933–6985 | 53 |
| 15 | Wiring helpers | 6986–7089 | 104 |
| 16 | Rotation-aware selection | 7090–7147 | 58 |
| 17 | Audit-tier selection | 7148–7307 | 160 |
| 18 | Implement-tier selection | 7308–7471 | 164 |
| 19 | Plan/intake selection | 7472–7510 | 39 |
| 20 | Critical-first selection | 7511–7804 | 294 |
| 21 | Dependency frontier resolution | 7805–7913 | 109 |
| 22 | Settings clamps | 7914–8034 | 121 |
| 23 | Round-robin helpers | 8035–8105 | 71 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Module-level mutable state:** `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` (line 2523)
  backs the per-process dispatch-pipeline single-flight gate.
- **Pre-existing coupling:** `stalled-work.ts` imports
  `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, `paneLabelItemId`
  and several types from `./downtime-worker.js`, while `downtime-worker.ts`
  imports `StalledPaneCandidate`, `StalledResumeOutcome` and `StalledScanOptions`
  types from `./stalled-work.js` — an existing type-only cycle that the split
  must not turn into a runtime cycle.
- **Precedent:** [WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO](../../../../.worklog) decomposed the
  2,584-line `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public
  API, tests passing without modification, and ≤500 lines per new module.

## Desired change

Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its contents
into cohesive sibling modules, each well under 1,000 lines. A starting
decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision, subject to the
constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.constants.ts` | Tuning constants, floors/maxima, `decisionHeaderToken` | ~420 |
| `downtime-worker.types.ts` | Exported interfaces and unions (`LlamaStatus`, candidates, claim/result types, config, worker) | ~700 |
| `downtime-worker.idle.ts` | Idle detection, idle-duration tracker, per-slot tracker | ~255 |
| `downtime-worker.poller.ts` | `parseLlamaStatus`, `fetchLocalStatus`, `createDowntimePoller` | ~284 |
| `downtime-worker.gates.ts` | Soft-delete/assignee holds, review-queue depth gate, audit batch status, `classifyItemForDispatch`, attempt budget, critical-only escape hatch | ~480 |
| `downtime-worker.selection.ts` | wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, rotation, critical-first, dependency frontier | ~830 |
| `downtime-worker.clamps.ts` | `clampDowntime*` settings normalisers | ~130 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.ts` | Pane args/spawn options/spawn, pane-lifecycle monitor | ~360 |
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` | Herdr list-head filter pipeline (`dispatchDowntimeWork`), prompt/comment builders | ~700–1,000 |

# Tests: herdr request-priority mappings & interactive dispatch

Test-first unit tests defining the herdr-side request-priority contract (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH), so implementation can proceed test-first.

## Goal
Executable specs for the two priority-mapping tables and for the interactive dispatch environment threading, in `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.test.ts` (plus the existing spawn/arg-builder tests).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Interactive mapping table:** a pure helper maps work-item `low` → `medium`, `medium` → `high`, `high` → `high`, `critical` → `high`; and maps an absent/unresolvable item (no id, lookup failure, timeout) → `high`.
- [ ] **Downtime mapping table:** a pure helper maps work-item `low` → `low`, `medium` → `medium`, `high` → `high`, `critical` → `high`; and maps an unknown/absent priority → `medium`.
- [ ] **Headless dispatch:** a test proves `spawnBackgroundPi` adds `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (already-mapped value) to the child process env, and that an unmapped/unresolvable dispatch defaults to `high`.
- [ ] **Pane arg/script contract:** a test proves the `send-to-pi.sh` argument builder forwards the request priority so the spawned pane process receives `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (the `exec env …` / `pane split --env` / `grid.py` passthrough form chosen during implementation).
- [ ] Tests reside next to the code they exercise and are initially red (new modules/arguments do not yet exist), so the implementation children can turn them green.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (headless/arg-builder coverage) or the existing spawn test module

## Notes
- Exact tables are fixed by the parent ACs; do not relax them.
- Fail-open is required: a lookup failure must never abort a dispatch.

# Tests: Pi extension X-Priority header injection

Test-first unit tests for the Worklog pi extension module that turns the pane-launch environment variable into the `X-Priority` provider request header (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC4).

## Goal
Executable specs in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts` covering valid, invalid and unset `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` values and the `before_provider_headers` hook registration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Valid values:** `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` of `low`, `medium` or `high` causes the hook to set `X-Priority` to that exact value on the outgoing header map.
- [ ] **Unset value:** with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` absent or empty, the header map is returned untouched (no `X-Priority` added; the proxy applies its own `medium` default).
- [ ] **Invalid value:** any other value (`fast`, `HIGH`, `critical`, whitespace, etc.) leaves the header map untouched.
- [ ] **Hook registration:** the extension module registers a `before_provider_headers` hook when loaded, and the hook is side-effect free when the env var is unset.
- [ ] Tests are colocated at `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts` and are initially red.

## Key Files
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts`

## Notes
- Fail-open is mandatory: a missing/invalid value must never inject an assumed `high`.
- Source of truth for the env contract is the parent description (`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, values `low|medium|high`).

Remove the client half of the retired fast/cheap operating mode and fix audit Phase-2 parallelism to serial (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC1/AC5).

## Goal
Herdr no longer contains or configures a mode-switch worker, sends no `/admin/set-mode` calls, exposes no `modeSwitch*` settings, and always runs audit Phase 2 serially; the plugin starts and dispatches normally.

# Implement: Pi Worklog extension injects X-Priority

Add the Worklog pi extension module that conveys pane-launch request priority to the LLM proxy (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC4).

## Goal
Every pi session herdr launches reads `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` and, when it is a valid priority, sets the `X-Priority` header on every provider request; otherwise it leaves headers untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.ts` validates `process.env.HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, accepting only `low`, `medium`, `high`, and sets the `X-Priority` request header via a `before_provider_headers` hook.

- [ ] The module is registered from `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts`.
- [ ] The F2 unit tests (valid/invalid/unset) pass; no proxy (`llm-manager`) change is made.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Add a small `resolveRequestPriority(env)` helper returning `low|medium|high|undefined`.
2. Register `before_provider_headers(ctx => ({...headers, ...(prio ? {'X-Priority': prio} : {})}))`.
3. Export/register the module from `index.ts`.
4. Rely on the proxy's own `medium` default when no header is sent.

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.ts` (new)

# Implement: herdr interactive dispatch priority

Resolve the dispatched work item's priority at interactive dispatch time and thread it to the pane/headless process as `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC2).

## Goal
Interactive agent panes and headless `spawnBackgroundPi` runs carry the mapped request priority of the work item they were dispatched for, so the proxy can serve urgent work responsively.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` exposes the interactive mapping (`low`→`medium`, `medium`/`high`/`critical`→`high`, unresolved→`high`) and the downtime mapping (`low`/`medium`/`high` unchanged, `critical`→`high`, unknown→`medium`) as pure, unit-tested helpers.
- [ ] `index.ts` resolves the dispatched item's work-item priority from the worklist item cache, falling back to a fail-open `wl show` lookup; a free-form `/prompt:`, missing id, lookup failure or timeout maps to `high` and still dispatches.
- [ ] Interactive agent panes and headless `spawnBackgroundPi` runs set `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` in the child env from the mapped priority.
- [ ] `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` forwards the request priority into the spawned pane process (e.g. `exec env HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=… bash run-pi-agent.sh …`, or `grid.py`/`pane split --env` passthrough on the resize path), with usage docs updated.
- [ ] `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` either mirrors the passthrough or documents that shell-command panes carry no priority context.
- [ ] The F1 mapping and dispatch tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Add the mapping helpers and unit-test them (F1 specs).
2. At the interactive dispatch seam, read the item's priority from the cached worklist item; else `wl show <id> --json` with a short timeout; default `high`.
3. Add `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` to the child env for panes and `spawnBackgroundPi`.
4. Update `send-to-pi.sh` (and `grid.py` if the resize path is used) to preserve the variable into the pane process.
5. Reuse `scrubRepositoryOverrides`-style env construction so the variable survives the launch.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`
- `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`

# Reduce time to run tests

**Headline:** Identify and eliminate redundant or slow tests across the vitest and pytest suites so the canonical suite (tests/cli + tests/unit) drops from ~8.5–12.7 minutes to ~6 minutes or less (≥30% wall-clock reduction), without meaningful coverage loss.

## Problem statement

Running the project's test suite takes a very long time. The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`, per `.pi/test-config.json`) recently takes **486–730 s for `tests/cli` alone** plus **22–28 s for `tests/unit`** (test-skill run cache, 2026-10-16→20), and the full vitest suite aggregates **~2434 s of test time across 8281 tests** (test-timings.json, 2026-10-20). The top 12 test files consume over 50% of aggregate runtime, and a single test (`read-cache-spawn-reduction`, a 6-pane simulation) takes **203 s**. Every implement/test/audit gate pays this cost, slowing agent and human delivery loops.

## Users

- **Primary:** Maintainers and agents running the test suite repeatedly for implement/test/audit gates and CI.
- **Secondary:** Contributors who need fast feedback on changed scope.

**User stories:**
- As a maintainer running the full suite, I want slow or redundant tests removed/optimised so each gate run is materially faster.
- As an agent on the test gate, I want the canonical suite to complete in minutes, not 10+ minutes, so I can iterate quickly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Baseline recorded:** A baseline is captured on a consistent (idle-ish) host using the canonical commands (`npm --silent test -- tests/cli`, `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`, plus full `npm --silent test`), with per-test timings produced via `npm run test:timings`; the top-20 slowest tests are identified and listed in a comment on the work item.
- **Measurable reduction:** The canonical suite wall-clock (tests/cli + tests/unit on the same host) is reduced by **≥30%** versus the recorded baseline.
- **Per-test triage:** Every test ≥5 s is triaged — mocked/stubbed external dependency, moved to an integration-only/long-run location, or retained with a documented justification comment. No test is silently ignored.
- **Redundancy removal:** Redundant, duplicated, or dead tests are removed with each removal accounted for (coverage preserved or explicitly migrated) in work-item comments; no meaningful coverage loss.
- **Python suite included:** pytest tests (`tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_*.py`) are measured and included in the same triage; slow python tests are optimised or justified.
- **Green gate:** The full project test suite passes with the changes and stays green across 3 consecutive CI-like runs without intermittent timeouts (traces the determinism constraint); a regression guard prevents reintroduction of a known worst offender if feasible.
- **Docs updated:** All related documentation updated to reflect the changes — code comments, the test-related section of `README.md`, and `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (post-change baseline numbers plus refreshed top-20 slow-test table); every updated doc is named in a work-item comment.

## Constraints

- No change to test behaviour semantics without a documented, coverage-preserving reason.
- Keep changes localised to test code and test config (vitest.config.ts, CI scripts) unless a production optimisation is the proven cause of a slow test.
- Tests must remain deterministic; the suite must run green 3× under CI-like conditions without intermittent timeouts.
- Python tests: keep pytest suite fast; do not break the audit-log/prune plugin coverage they provide.

## Existing state

- **Frameworks:** Vitest (TS/JS, `tests/` + `packages/`) and pytest (Python, `tests/test_*.py`).
- **Canonical suite** (`.pi/test-config.json`): `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`.
- **Recent canonical runtimes** (test-skill cache, green runs): tests/cli 183–785 s (median ~450 s; current ~660 s), tests/unit 7–41 s (median ~15 s).
- **Full suite aggregate:** 2434 s across 8281 tests; top files: read-cache-spawn-reduction (203 s), sync-vs-mutation (163 s), read-cache-e2e (146 s), close-recursive (128 s), init (109 s), issue-management (96 s), issue-status (75 s), startup-import-budget (73 s), valid-json-output (69 s), entry-point-split (67 s), install-herdr tests (67 s), json-output-shape (63 s). Slowest single tests: 203 s read-cache spawn-reduction, 69 s startup-import-budget, 47 s entry-point-split, 42 s sync-integration-convergence, ~26 s read-cache-e2e variants, ~20 s github-push-synced-items, ~16 s sync-assignee-clear, 13.4 s herdr build-guard (tsc).
- **Known trends:** transform/import overhead grows with per-file isolation (downtime-worker split measured +146% transform, +267% import). CLI suite runtime approximately doubled between 2026-10-17 (~180–280 s) and 2026-10-19–20 (~486–730 s), coinciding with read-cache, sync, and startup-budget test additions.

## Desired change

- Produce and publish a timings baseline; triage the top offenders; remove redundant/dead tests (with coverage accounting); mock/stub external dependencies (spawned `wl` processes, real git syncs, heavy setup) where feasible; move long-running integration tests to a separate long-run/CI group; apply the same treatment to pytest.
- Target: canonical suite wall-clock reduced ≥30%.

## Execution order (plan handoff)

Baseline (AC1) → triage the ≥5 s tests (AC3) → mock/optimise the proven offenders → remove redundancy with accounting (AC4) → pytest pass (AC5) → doc updates (AC7) → green-gate verification 3× (AC6) → post-change comparison versus baseline (AC2). AC1 must complete before any optimisation work so every later change is measured against a recorded baseline.

## Plan: changelog

  - Handoff: added the execution-order line above.
  - Sequencing/scope-sizing: no children exist, so no dependency or sizing changes were needed (coverage review reported `proceed`).

- WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B — Investigate transient wl process CPU usage (in-progress; read-cache/startup test family).
- WL-0MSGAE35E001557V — Read-cache core module (completed; source of the read-cache e2e/spawn-reduction tests).
- WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN — Startup import-budget harness and baseline (completed; source of the 69 s startup-import-budget test).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. Q: Current test run time? Have skills left logs? — A (producer, interactive): "I do not know, don't skills leave logs?" — Research: the test skill's per-repo run cache (`.worklog/cache/`) records every full-suite run. Recent canonical green runs: tests/cli 486–730 s, tests/unit 22–28 s → canonical ~510–760 s total. Full suite aggregates 2434 s test-time across 8281 tests (test-timings.json, 2026-10-20). Baseline accepted from skill logs.
2. Q: Scope (canonical/full/specific area)? — A: both — canonical and full suite; no specific area, "just aiming for faster."
3. Q: New work beyond prior slow-CLI refactor? — A: review the work done, look for additional improvement opportunities.
4. Q: Approach (remove / optimise / both / other)? — A: c — both remove redundant/dead tests and optimise slow tests.
5. Q: Python (pytest) tests in scope? — A: yes — tests/test_audit_runner_core.py, tests/test_install_audit_log_hygiene.py, tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py, tests/conftest.py.

**Assumptions:** target ≥30% canonical wall-clock reduction vs recorded baseline (no explicit number supplied); timing is host-dependent so baseline must be re-measured on a consistent host before/after.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Host-load noise:** absolute timings are host/load-dependent (shared 16-core host); mitigations: measure baseline and post-change on the same host, use median of ≥3 runs, record load average.
- **Coverage loss on removal:** a removed test may carry unique coverage; mitigation: per-removal accounting (work-item comments), rely on full suite green + coverage review.
- **Flakiness from mocking:** replacing real git/process spawns with mocks can introduce false confidence; mitigation: keep at least one real integration test per subsystem, move to long-run group rather than delete.
- **Scope creep:** parallelisation, CI sharding, and test-infra rewrites are attractive but out of scope; record as linked follow-up work items, not this brief.
- **Recent runtime inflation correlates with read-cache/sync/startup test additions** (CLI suite ~2× Oct 17→Oct 20); a quick win may be reworking these to shared fixtures or fewer spawns, but assume nothing until the triage pass measures it.

# Audit-batch dispatch — test specs (test-first)

Test-first companion to WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS. Write the FAILING test specs for depth-aware audit batching BEFORE any implementation. The specs pin the behaviours in parent AC1–AC5 so the implementation items (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS children C3–C5) verify against them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC6: Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.

- `downtime-worker.settings.test.ts`: `clampDowntimeAuditBatchMax` clamps to [1, 5], non-finite falls back to the default (2), `1` = legacy/off; `loadSettings` parses `downtimeAuditBatchMax` from a fixture config (valid, invalid, missing).
- `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` (parent AC6a): shallow depth (< `browseItemCount`) keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour — exactly one dispatch and a full idle-tracker reset (`tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])`) after it, and no `audit-batch-continue` token.
- `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6b): depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces exactly N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window, each continuation gated by a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check.
- `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6c): an unsatisfied idle-duration gate and sub-2 free slots block ALL dispatch including continuations; `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` is never relaxed.
- `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6d): a non-stale host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation; the continuation proceeds only after the marker is released.
- `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` / `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (AC6e, AC6f, AC4): the cap and the depth-drop end the batch and restore single-dispatch behaviour; dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice; a failed CAS claim / spawn failure / any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch; in coordination mode the leader defers the own-backlog leadership hand-off until batch end.
- Every spec is runnable against the current tree (red) — each uses only the current public API (dispatch functions, worker object, settings loaders) and existing fixture/stub patterns.

# Depth-derived batch activation + conditional idle reset in `tick()`

Core of parent AC1/AC2/AC3: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head, activate a bounded batch budget only when the queue is deep, and replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one scoped strictly to an audit-batch continuation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC1: Depth-aware batching: an audit-eligible depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` above 1 allows distinct audit continuations inside one idle window until the cap or the depth drop.
- Covers parent AC2: Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.
- Covers parent AC3: No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.

- **Depth computation (AC1).** A helper derives the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head: count items where `classifyItemForDispatch(item, now) === 'audit'` (root `completed`/`in_review`, excluding fresh-audited, producer-review, assignee-held and soft-deleted items). No new `wl` subprocess is added to the common dispatch path.
- **Activation rule (AC1).** Batch mode is active only when `depth >= browseItemCount` AND `auditBatchMax > 1`; otherwise behaviour is byte-for-byte today's: one dispatch per idle window followed by a full idle-tracker reset.
- **Batch budget state (AC1/AC3).** An in-memory per-worker budget (like `lastDispatchAt`/`cooldownUntil`) counts audit dispatches in the current batch, is initialised to `auditBatchMax` when a batch activates, and is cleared when: the cap is reached, the depth drops below the threshold, a non-audit dispatch occurs, an audit dispatch ends in any non-`dispatched` outcome (including `claim-failed`, `claim-rolled-back`, `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed`, `anchor-unavailable`), the worker pauses/cooldowns, or leadership is lost.
- **Conditional idle reset (AC2).** On a successful **audit** dispatch while a batch is active with budget remaining, `tick()` does NOT call `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])`; for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, today's reset is preserved exactly. Every gate (idle-duration threshold, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, `slotOwned`, `contention_queue_depth == 0`, code-freeze, host-wide/per-worklog audit markers, single-flight) is still re-checked on every tick, including continuations — no gate is relaxed or bypassed.
- **No duplicate / no target skipping (AC3).** Continuations flow through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A continuation never skips to a different target after a failed outcome — the batch simply ends.
- **Regression safety.** Non-audit dispatch (critical/implement/plan/intake/risk-effort) still resets the tracker and never arms a batch even when the queue is deep; legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`) keeps its existing tier-chain semantics.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `computeAuditEligibleDepth(items, now)` (or equivalent) beside `readReviewQueueGate` in `downtime-worker.ts`; reuse `classifyItemForDispatch` — no second eligibility definition.
- Add `auditBatch` worker-scope state (cap, remaining, active flag) and a `shouldDeferIdleReset(outcome, depth, cap)` decision helper (pure, exported for tests).
- In `tick()`: after a successful dispatch, look at `outcome.kind === 'audit'`, the current depth and the remaining budget, then conditionally skip the reset; clear the budget on every batch-ending condition listed in AC3.
- Extend `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` with the minimal machine-readable surface the worker needs (e.g. `auditBatchEligible?: boolean`), documented in the interface comment.
- Cover with the specs from C1 plus any new unit tests for the pure helpers.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the settings/plumbing item (C2) for `auditBatchMax`.

## Deliverables

- Depth helper + batch budget + conditional reset, with green audit-tier/dispatch/orchestrator tests.

# Coordination-mode batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

Parent AC4: on the production coordination path the leader must source continuation audit targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking) without releasing leadership mid-batch, and defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC2: Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.
- Covers parent AC3: No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.
- Covers parent AC4: Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

- **Continuation source (AC4).** After a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, `dispatchFromCoordination` may dispatch the next audit target from the leader's own head extension (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `includeNonCritical` filter as today) instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion — still exactly one dispatch per invocation, never two.
- **Same filters (AC3/AC4).** Every own-head continuation passes the identical sequential filters as the existing own-backlog fallback: `classifyItemForDispatch`, dispatched-marker exclusion (id-guard + staleness), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, audit slot minimum (≥2), in-flight critical guard, review-queue hold for implements. The continuation selects only `audit`-kind items.
- **No duplicate target (AC3).** The item just dispatched, and any item already dispatched in this batch, is never re-selected in the same batch — enforced by the existing marker exclusion plus an explicit batch-local exclusion set, covered by a test.
- **Leadership timing (AC4).** An own-backlog (`ownBacklogDispatch === true`) audit dispatch during an active batch with budget remaining does NOT trigger `releaseLeadership()` in that tick; the step-down happens exactly once at batch end (cap reached, depth dropped, failed continuation, or the next tick when the batch is no longer active). A normal in-view dispatch is unchanged.
- **No regression.** Non-batch coordination dispatch, leader election/lease TTL, coordination check-ins, pruning and the offer path are unchanged; `dispatchFromCoordination` direct-API callers without `freeSlots`/`auditBatchMax` keep today's behaviour (fail-open).

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread `auditBatchMax` and the batch-continuation intent through `dispatchFromCoordination`'s options (a boolean/marker set by `tick()` when the batch is active, plus the dispatched-target set for the current batch).
- Factor the existing own-backlog candidate loop into a reusable helper so the continuation path applies the exact same filters (no duplicated filter chain).
- Add `auditBatchContinuation?: boolean` (and any needed batch metadata) to `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`, documented, so `tick()` can decide the leadership step-down and the idle-reset deferral without re-deriving state.
- In `tick()`, gate the existing `outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true` step-down on batch-inactive (deferring it to batch end).
- Cover with the coordination-dispatch and orchestrator specs from C1.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and outcome surface.
- Depends on the observability item (C5) for the continuation token contract.

## Deliverables

- Leader own-head continuation with unchanged filter semantics and deferred step-down, with green coordination-dispatch/orchestrator tests.
