# Observability: audit-batch decision tokens and metadata

Parent AC5: every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log at the existing rate limit. Existing reason tokens are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC5: Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

- **Continuation token (AC5).** An accepted audit-batch continuation records a distinct token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`) in the existing decision log with metadata: `depth`, `cap`, `remaining`, plus today's standard fields (`freeSlots`, `totalSlots`, `ownerPresent`, `runningPanes`, `contentionDepth`).
- **Blocked continuation tokens (AC5).** Held/blocked continuations reuse the existing tokens unchanged — `audit-in-flight` (per-worklog single-flight) and `audit-host-saturated` (host-wide marker) for marker blocks, `slot-owned`, `proxy-contention`, `code-freeze`, `review-queue-hold`, `no-candidate` — with the batch metadata (depth/cap/remaining) attached when a batch was active.
- **Batch end observability.** Batch deactivation transitions that would otherwise be silent surface in the decision log where a distinct signal adds value (e.g. cap reached / depth dropped) without spamming the log — still rate-limited by `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`.
- **Rate limiting + header unchanged.** The header blocking token updates on every refusal exactly as today; `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` behaviour is preserved for refusals; no existing reason-token test regresses.
- **Doc alignment.** The new/attached tokens match the token list committed in the docs item (C6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the decision-log entry shape (`CoordinationLogEntry` kind `decision`) with optional `batch?: { depth: number; cap: number; remaining: number }` + the `audit-batch-continue`/`audit-batch-held`(if distinct signal) reasons routed through the worker's `recordDecision`.
- Emit the continuation token from `tick()` after a batch-armed continuation attempt (accepted or held) with the live depth/cap/remaining; re-compute depth from the head the same way as C3.
- Update the reason-token comment blocks in `downtime-worker.ts` and the dispatcher doc token list (§~60/108).

# Documentation: batch setting, activation rule, sequential-safety invariants and decision tokens

# Intake Brief — Reduce per-invocation cost of the transient `wl` processes (WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B)

## Problem statement (headline)

Every `wl` command spawns a fresh Node.js process that takes **0.6–1.7 s and 80–180 MB** just to boot (a bare `node -e ''` is 0.35 s / 58 MB): the CLI eagerly imports 40+ modules (commander, all ~35 command builders, plugins, runtime, `better-sqlite3`) before any command logic, and herdr panes + pi agents fire these one-shot processes continuously (30 s refresh ticks, 60 s `sync --if-idle` per pane, per-agent polls). Four concurrent `wl` processes were observed at 25–65 % CPU each — bursty, seconds-long, gone moments later. The shipped read-cache (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3) cut *read work* (83 %) but deliberately left process spawning unchanged ("each invocation still spawns a wl process"). There is also an unbounded hygiene leak: `~/.cache/wl/state/` holds **216,228 one-file-per-worklog-dir counters (~890 MB, 216k inodes)** that are never pruned.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI panes / pi agents** — the heaviest spawners; every 30–60 s tick pays full process boot even for cache hits.
  - *As a herdr pane, I want cache-hit refreshes to cost near bare-node boot, so refresh cycles stop stealing core-seconds from the host.*
- **Operators / agents running ad-hoc `wl` commands** — every `wl create/update/comment/sync/next` pays the same boot cost.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl` commands to feel instant, so interactive and agent-driven use stops producing CPU bursts.*
- **Host administrators** — transient process bursts and an unbounded 890 MB cache dir degrade a shared Raspberry Pi / herdr server.
  - *As an admin, I want spawn load and cache disk bounded, so the host stays responsive.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **(AC1)** **Import budget on the fast path:** the cache-hit read path and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins. Measured on the reference host (this repo, node ≥ 20): p95 wall time for a warm repeated `wl next --json` / `list --status open --json` cache hit ≤ **0.5 s** and peak RSS ≤ **60 MB** (current: ~0.6–1.2 s / 80–160 MB; bare node 0.35 s / 58 MB — the margin is deliberately tiny, so the fast-path import set must be slimmer than today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 61 MB). Enforced by a regression benchmark/test (e.g. asserts the heavy modules are not imported on the fast path).
- **(AC2)** **Measurable spawn-load reduction:** total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across ≥ 4 panes on one shared worklog dir drops **≥ 60 %** versus current behaviour, measured by extending the env-gated spawn instrumentation (`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, src/spawn-counter.ts) to record per-process CPU time (`process.resourceUsage().user+system`); baseline and after numbers quoted in the work item.
- **(AC3)** **Cache hygiene / bounded on-disk state:** `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files, ~890 MB, one file per worklog dir ever seen) is bounded and prunable — after a run, state storage is capped (bounded file count, or consolidated storage) and stale entries are removed; a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it. Freshness semantics unchanged (no correctness regression).
- **(AC4)** **No correctness regression:** all read-cache invariants from WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 hold — write→read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers/writers, byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version). The existing read-cache/e2e/spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.
- **(AC5)** **Graceful degradation:** if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI (no functional regression, help/plugin registration intact).
- **(AC6)** **Tests + docs:** unit/integration/benchmark tests cover the fast path, lazy loading, CPU-time instrumentation and cache hygiene; related documentation (CLI.md / CONFIG.md / docs as appropriate) updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Stateless one-shot CLI** — no daemon, no long-lived server, no IPC worker (operator decision, Q1-A). Architecture and on-disk Git/JSONL sync semantics must not change.
- `wl` must keep working from any worktree/`--worklog-dir` (the prefix-to-sibling resolution and worklog-dir override must not be disturbed by splitting the entry point).
- Cache correctness invariants (WAL aware, TTL 30 s, LRU bound) are **non-negotiable** — the fast path only shortens import time.
- Node ESM, build via `tsc` to `dist/`; `/usr/local/bin/wl` symlinks into this repo's `dist/cli.js` (v1.0.22) — keep that contract intact.
- Performance benchmarks must be CPU-time based / tolerant on shared hosts (a Raspberry Pi, herdr server).

## Existing state

- Read-cache epic **shipped (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3, v1.0.9)**: identical JSON reads (list/next/show/search/status) served pre-parse from `~/.cache/wl` with 83 % read-work reduction, sync+heartbeat, herdr in-process memoisation. Its audit records the accepted variance: "each invocation still spawns a wl process that exits without DB work" — the spawn itself was left in scope.
- pi-extension poll gating shipped (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N + tests WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5); orphaned worktree process lifecycle shipped (WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO).
- Herdr cadence: 30 s refresh × 4–5 wl fetches per pane, 60 s auto-sync with 45 s cross-instance heartbeat (packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts).
- Measured here: `node -e ''` 0.35 s/58 MB; `wl --version` 0.95 s/80 MB; `wl list --json` (repeated) 0.6–1.2 s/80–160 MB; `wl status` 1.74 s/180 MB; `wl sync --if-idle` 1.39 s/116 MB; importing `dist/cli-utils.js` alone 0.60 s/73 MB; `dist/read-cache-cli.js` 0.46 s/61 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Split the entry point:** keep `src/cli.ts` thin — argv scan + read-cache fast path (imports only `read-cache-cli`, `spawn-counter`, `worklog-paths` + minimal utils), then **dynamically import** the current heavy graph (`./cli-main.ts` or lazy command map). Cache hits and `--version` exit before commander/DB/plugins load.
2. **Lazy per-command imports:** replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a registry resolving each command on demand; `--help` / bare invocation may load all (rare).
3. **Extend spawn instrumentation** with per-process CPU time (ru_utime/ru_stime) to measure CPU-second reduction, not just spawn count.
4. **Cache hygiene:** bound/prune `~/.cache/wl/state/` (e.g. LRU/TTL over counter files, consolidate counters, housekeeping in `wl doctor`); optionally tidy stale top-level entries.
5. **If ≥60 % CPU-second reduction is not reached by import slimming alone** (spawn count unchanged), coalesce repeated herdr reads into fewer wl invocations (still stateless, e.g. one batch query per refresh tick) — record which lever was needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli.ts` — split entry: 40 eager imports (lines ~6–47), cache fast path (~526–545) that currently runs only after the full graph loads.
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — cache lookup/backfill/invalidation orchestration; the fast-path import set.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — `state/` counter files (`stateCounterFilePath`/`bumpStateCounter`, ~157–200), purge/LRU, entry layout.
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — extend `SpawnRecord` with CPU time.
- `src/commands/*.ts` — command modules to lazy-load (next, list, status, show, search, sync, …).
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`, `src/cli-utils.ts`, `src/lib/runtime.ts` — heavy imports to defer.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — cache maintenance command (state pruning).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — coalescing repeated reads per refresh tick (only if needed to hit AC2).
- Tests: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`, new `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` / CPU-time benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (completed, v1.0.7) — "Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM)"** — the predecessor investigation. It attacked spawn *count* (pi browse-widget idle-gating → WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N, herdr cadence, read-cache). **Not a duplicate:** it left per-invocation *cost* and on-disk cache hygiene untouched; this item targets boot cost + `state/` growth.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (completed) — read-cache epic; the spawn cost was its accepted variance; this item continues from there.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N / WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5 (completed) — visibility-gated polling in pi extension / herdr (spawn-count side).
- WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO (completed) — orphaned node process lifecycle in worktrees.
- WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY (completed) — process lifecycle documentation (reference for docs conventions).
- WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13 (completed) — metrics collection module (host metric collection precedent; candidate to reuse for CPU-second reporting).
- WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K (completed) — `wl sync` before refactor/standup skills (lock-aware `sync --if-idle` spawners).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/in-progress item targeting wl startup cost; `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` covers the already-shipped spawn-count remediation only.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lazy/help registration risk:** commander help and plugin registration must not regress — mitigated by AC5 fallback and deferring full registration to the heavy path.
- **Entry-point tests:** several suites import `src/cli.ts` / `dist/cli.js` directly; splitting must keep those contracts (tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts, inproc-harness, smoke, completion, …).
- **Benchmark flakiness** on shared hosts — AC1/AC2 measured by CPU time, p95 over repeated runs, generous margins above bare-node baseline.
- **State-dir pruning races:** pruning counters concurrently with writers must stay atomic (temp+rename, no regression of counter monotonicity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** daemon/server mode, JSONL/Git sync changes, and TUI redesign are explicitly out of scope — recorded as related opportunities, not work here.
- **Assumption:** the reference-host measurements above are representative of the failing hosts (same repo/worklog versions; herdr panes are the dominant spawner).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What's the target shape of the improvement?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — keep `wl` a stateless one-shot CLI; lazy per-command imports, fast path for cache hits/`--version` at near-node-boot cost, plus cache hygiene (prune `state/`, bound growth). No daemon.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — "How should we measure success?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle ≥ 60 % reduction; per-process RSS < 60 MB; no correctness regression.** Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: measured per-invocation cost (0.6–1.7 s / 80–180 MB vs 0.35 s / 58 MB bare node), attributed to eager 40-module import graph; verified the read-cache fast path still loads the full graph before serving (src/cli.ts); confirmed unbounded `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files / ~890 MB) with no pruning path.

## Related work (automated report)

Collected by `/skill:find-related` (sidecar: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B.md`).

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY** — Documentation for process lifecycle management (completed)
- **WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13** — Metrics collection module (completed)
- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr cadence/spawner documentation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher/claim spawn context
- `CHANGELOG.md` — historical process-spawn/read-cache entries


---

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-19)

Phasing is vertical slices (tracer bullets): measurement first, then the entry-point fast path, then cache hygiene, then the CPU-second verdict and docs. Each slice covers its own code, tests and docs; between phases, review the next items' descriptions and re-check the measured numbers.

| # | Child | Title | Type | Est. | Depends on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19 | Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS | feature | S | — | Measure CPU-time and RSS per spawn (AC1 RSS, AC2) |
| F2 | WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN | Startup import-budget harness and baseline | feature | S | F1 | Ratchet + benchmark that lock in AC1 and capture the baseline |
| F3 | WL-0MVFRRCP7007UWS7 | Tests: thin entry-point split and dispatch parity | task | S | F2 | Test-first contracts for the entry split |
| F4 | WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ | Split CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamic heavy graph | feature | M | F3 | Fast path exits before commander/DB/plugins load (AC1) |
| F5 | WL-0MVFRREMZ0085G7I | Tests: lazy command registry, help and plugin fidelity | task | S | F4 | Test-first contracts incl. AC5 fallback |
| F6 | WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3 | Lazy per-command imports via command registry | feature | M | F5 | Load only the command that runs (AC1, AC5) |
| F7 | WL-0MVFRROLM002K98B | Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget | feature | M | F2, F4, F6 | Meet and freeze the AC1 numbers |
| F8 | WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1 | Tests: cache state pruning, bounds and atomicity | task | S | — | Test-first contracts for AC3 hygiene + AC4 freshness |
| F9 | WL-0MVFRRQ9W003KEFL | Bound and prune cache state via wl doctor cache | feature | M | F8 | Bounded `state/` store + documented maintenance path (AC3) |
| F10 | WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J | Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle | feature | M | F1, F6, F7 | AC2 measurement and herdr-coalescing verdict |
| F11 | WL-0MVFRRTY5001KTNH | Docs: fast path, instrumentation and cache maintenance | docs | XS | F1, F7, F9 | AC6 documentation half |

### Plan-stage decisions (recorded assumptions)

- **D1 — Budget enforcement is a ratchet, not a single hard-coded threshold.** AC1's 0.5 s / 60 MB budget is tighter than today's fast-path graph (0.46 s / 61 MB), so F2 checks in a budget file (`bench/startup-import-budget.json`) that records the statically reachable graph and the measured cost, and fails on growth. F4 and F7 tighten it in the change that improves it — keeping the suite green between items while locking in every improvement and making the regression test deterministic and host-load tolerant.
- **D2 — Peak RSS comes from the instrumented child.** `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` is recorded per process by F1, so AC1's RSS check needs no external sampler.
- **D3 — Cache hygiene uses a bounded LRU plus TTL over `state/*.json`.** Consolidating counters into the cache entry files is only adopted if the bounded-file approach misses AC3's cap, because the counter atomicity and monotonicity invariant (`bumpStateCounter`) is the freshness guarantee and must not be rebuilt.
- **D4 — Herdr coalescing is conditional, not assumed.** Desired change #5 is gated behind F10's measurement because herdr already dedupes concurrent identical reads (in-flight memo, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) and serves default-view reads in-process via `@worklog/shared` (WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B). The expected remaining gap is per-spawn boot cost.
- **D5 — `--version` uses the generated `src/version.ts`.** `getVersion()` currently lives in the 73 MB `cli-utils` graph; the fast path reads `WORKLOG_VERSION` directly so `wl --version` can exit at bare-node cost.
- **D6 — No daemon, no sync/JSONL changes** (intake Q1-A): the fast path changes only *when* modules load, never what is cached or how sync works.

### Appendix: planning-stage questions and decisions

Intake already recorded Q1 (stateless one-shot CLI, lazy imports, cache hygiene) and Q2 (CPU-second measurement, under 60 MB RSS, no correctness regression). The plan stage asked no new questions: the intake brief's measurements, desired-change list and answered decisions left no ambiguous choice that would change the decomposition. D1–D6 are recorded as assumptions for audit rather than as invented requirements.

- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking):** if F7 cannot reach 60 MB peak RSS (bare node is already 58 MB), should AC1's RSS limit become "within 3 MB of bare node", or should the fast path be allowed further Node startup work (e.g. a compile cache or snapshot)? F7 raises this with measured evidence rather than silently relaxing the AC.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — plan skill: decomposed into 11 child items (F1–F11) in test-first dependency order; created all children at `stage=intake_complete`; wired 15 dependency edges; recorded decisions D1–D6; effort/risk re-estimated from the child WBS.

# F1 — Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU time and peak RSS

Extends the env-gated spawn instrumentation (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA) so each `wl` process records its own CPU time and peak RSS. This is the measurement lever for parent AC2 (CPU-seconds per refresh cycle) and for the RSS half of parent AC1.

## Target outcome

`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE` records gain `cpuMs` (user+system from `process.resourceUsage()`) and `maxRssKb`, so a coordinator can total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle and read per-process peak memory without an external sampler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SpawnRecord` carries `cpuMs` and `maxRssKb`; `recordSpawn()` appends `<kind>	<ts>	<pid>	<cpuMs>	<maxRssKb>`.
- Back-compat: 3-field legacy lines still parse, with CPU/RSS reported as `null` (not 0, so aggregation cannot silently under-report).
- `summariseSpawnRecords(file)` returns total records, per-kind counts, total CPU-seconds and max RSS over the file; covered by unit tests.
- Instrumentation stays best-effort: no throw and no behaviour change when the env vars are unset or the file is unwritable.
- `WL_SPAWN_COUNT=1` (stderr path) also reports CPU/RSS.
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` passes unchanged (kind counts unaffected).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Capture `process.resourceUsage()` at record time (`userCPUTime`/`systemCPUTime` are microseconds, `maxRSS` is KiB) and write the extended line.
2. Tolerate both line shapes in `readSpawnRecords()`.
3. Add the aggregation helper plus unit tests.

**Key Files:**
- `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- `tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Extended instrumentation, aggregation helper and unit tests.
- A baseline comment on the parent recording CPU-seconds and p95 wall/RSS for `wl next --json`, `wl list --json`, `wl status`, `wl sync --if-idle` and `wl --version`.

# F2 — Startup import-budget harness (ratchet) and baseline capture

Builds the verification harness for parent AC1 without breaking the green tree: a checked-in budget/ratchet that records the current fast-path import graph and measured cost, which later items tighten. Also captures the pre-change baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `bench/startup-import-budget.json` records (a) the set of modules statically reachable from `src/cli.ts`, (b) measured p95 wall time and peak RSS baselines for warm `wl next --json`, `wl list --status open --json` and `wl --version`, and (c) the parent AC1 target values (p95 <= 0.5 s, peak RSS <= 60 MB).
- **Ratchet test (always on, under one second):** walking static imports from `src/cli.ts` transitively, the test fails when a module is added to the graph. Removing modules is allowed and must be accompanied by a deliberate budget-file update, so every improvement is locked in and no regression slips through.
- **Regression test in the default suite:** measured p95 wall time stays within the recorded budget plus documented headroom; measurement is CPU-time based (`process.resourceUsage` via F1 spawn records) so a loaded shared host does not produce false failures, and the AC1 target is asserted once F4/F7 record it as the budget.
- **Reference-host report:** a benchmark script emits `--json` (p95 wall, peak RSS, CPU time, bare-node floor) for quoting in work-item comments; the exact command is documented so it can be re-run after F7.
- The harness works for both `src/` (tsx) and `dist/` (built) invocation, because `/usr/local/bin/wl` runs `dist/cli.js`, and for a served cache hit.
- Covers parent AC1's import budget: cache-hit reads and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins; the recorded budget tracks the reference-host p95 wall time <= 0.5 s and peak RSS <= 60 MB for warm `wl next --json` / `wl list --status open --json` cache hits.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`: transitive static-import walk of `src/cli.ts` compared with the budget file, plus the timing regression assertion against the recorded budget.
2. `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`: repeated warm runs (>= 10), p95 wall time, CPU time and RSS from F1 spawn records, bare-node floor reference, `--json` output.
3. `npm run benchmark:wl-startup` script entry.
4. Baseline comment on the parent with the measured numbers.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`
- `bench/startup-import-budget.json`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`
- `src/cli.ts`
- `package.json`

## Dependencies

- F1 (spawn records carry CPU time and RSS).

# F5 — Tests: lazy command registry, help and plugin fidelity

Test-first coverage for the lazy per-command registry (F6), including the parent AC5 graceful-degradation fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts that a normal command (`wl show <id> --json`) does not import unrelated command modules (static assertion on the registry's dynamic-import map, or a module-load sentinel).
- `--help` and bare `wl` still list all built-in commands in the grouped layout with global options, compared against the current output (plugin entries excluded from the snapshot).
- Plugin registration still runs on the heavy path (`loadPlugins`) and plugin commands appear in help.
- Fallback (parent AC5): when registry resolution fails (missing module or rejecting import), the CLI falls back to eager full registration and the command still runs; covered by a fault-injection test that mocks a rejecting dynamic import.
- Unknown commands keep the current error and exit behaviour (snapshot).
- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` and `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts` pass unchanged.
- Covers parent AC5: if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI — no functional regression, help and plugin registration intact.


**Key Files:**
- `tests/cli/lazy-command-registry.test.ts`
- `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts`
- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`
- `src/commands/*.ts`

## Dependencies

- F4 (split entry point in place).

# F8 — Tests: cache state pruning, bounds and atomicity

Test-first coverage for parent AC3 (bounded, prunable `~/.cache/wl/state/`) and for the freshness invariants pruning must not break (parent AC4). Today `state/<sha256(dir)>.json` is one file per worklog dir ever seen (216,228 files, about 890 MB on the reference host) with no pruning path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pruning tests cover: counters older than the TTL are removed; file count is capped at a configured bound (LRU by mtime) after a run; fresh and recently written counters are never removed.
- Atomicity/concurrency: pruning tolerates concurrent `bumpStateCounter` writers; a concurrent-writer test (pattern from `tests/read-cache-concurrent-child.ts`) asserts counter monotonicity and that a prune cannot reset a live counter.
- Freshness invariants unchanged: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts` and `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` pass unchanged (write-to-read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, byte-identical JSON).
- Bounded-state test: after 2x the bound of synthetic worklog dirs, `state/` holds no more than the bound and the cache still serves correct hits for surviving dirs.
- `wl doctor cache` behaviour is covered by CLI tests (exit code, `--json` shape, dry-run versus prune).
- Covers parent AC4: no correctness regression — write-to-read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers and writers, and byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version); the existing read-cache, e2e and spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.


**Key Files:**
- `tests/read-cache.test.ts`
- `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`
- `tests/read-cache-concurrent-child.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`
- `tests/cli/doctor-cache.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None (can start immediately after F2's baseline capture).

# F4 — Split the CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamically imported heavy graph

Implements desired change #1: `src/cli.ts` becomes a thin bootstrap (argv scan, read-cache fast path, `--version`) that dynamically imports the current heavy graph (`src/cli-main.ts`) only when a cache hit did not serve the invocation. This is the largest single lever for parent AC1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli.ts` statically imports only the fast-path allowlist; `commander`, command modules, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime` and `better-sqlite3` load only through dynamic `import()` inside `cli-main.ts`.
- The F2 budget file is tightened in the same change: the recorded fast-path graph becomes the allowlist, so a future eager import fails the ratchet test.
- A served cache hit exits before any heavy module loads; `wl --version` prints the version from `src/version.ts` and exits without heavy imports.
- Every command behaves identically: full suite green, including `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` and `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` unchanged (parent AC4).
- Cache semantics untouched: cache key/argv extraction, TTL/LRU, WAL-aware invalidation, write-to-read freshness and byte-identical JSON (parent AC4).
- Worktree detection/process registration and the `--worklog-dir` override still run on whichever path executes; no regression for `wl` inside a worktree.
- The `/usr/local/bin/wl` → `dist/cli.js` contract is preserved; `npm run build` emits both `dist/cli.js` and `dist/cli-main.js`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Move the current program construction, registration, help formatting, plugin loading and runtime initialisation into `src/cli-main.ts`, exporting an async `main(argv)`.
2. Keep argv normalisation, read-cache lookup, spawn recording and version printing in `src/cli.ts`; otherwise `await import('./cli-main.js')`.
3. Keep the write-invalidation hook on the shared path so writes still bump the state counter.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/cli-main.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `src/version.ts`
- `src/process-lifecycle.ts`
- `src/worklog-paths.ts`

## Dependencies

- F3 (tests first).
data.title: Split CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamic heavy graph

# F6 — Lazy per-command imports via a command registry

Implements desired change #2: replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a name → `() => import('./commands/x.js')` registry, resolved on demand. Only the command that actually runs loads its module; `--help` and bare `wl` may load all (rare).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli-main.ts` registers commands through the registry; no static imports of `./commands/*` remain.
- A single-command invocation loads only that command module (verified by F5's isolation test); `--help` and bare `wl` load all command modules and produce identical grouped help output.
- Plugin loading and `initializeRuntime` ordering is unchanged for commands that need them; commands that do not touch the DB still avoid opening it (visible in F1 spawn record kinds).
- Graceful degradation (parent AC5): a registry resolution error logs one warning, falls back to eager full registration, then dispatches the command; covered by F5's fault-injection test.
- Full suite green; existing read-cache, e2e and spawn-reduction suites unchanged (parent AC4).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Declare a registry mapping each name in the existing `builtInCommandNames` set to a dynamic import of its module.
2. Resolve the single command token from argv before `program.parse()` and register only that command (falling back to all for `--help`/bare invocation/unknown token).
3. Keep help grouping metadata independent of module loading.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli-main.ts`
- `src/command-registry.ts`
- `src/commands/*.ts`
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`

## Dependencies

- F5 (tests first).

# F7 — Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget

Parent AC1 sets a deliberately tight budget: p95 <= 0.5 s wall and <= 60 MB peak RSS for warm cache hits, against a bare-node floor of 0.35 s / 58 MB and today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 0.46 s / 61 MB. After F4/F6 the fast path still imports the read-cache graph, so this item shaves it until the budget is met and then freezes the win.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Warm cache-hit `wl next --json`, `wl list --status open --json` and `wl --version` on the reference host: p95 wall <= 0.5 s and peak RSS <= 60 MB (F2 benchmark, >= 10 runs), with before and after numbers quoted in a comment.
- The fast-path graph no longer imports `commander`, `better-sqlite3`, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime`, `config` or schema/validation plumbing; the F2 ratchet is tightened and its budget updated to the parent AC1 target (p95 <= 0.5 s, peak RSS <= 60 MB).
- The specific reductions are recorded (for example: version read from `src/version.ts`, minimal worklog-dir resolution on the fast path, hashing/crypto deferred to the miss path, argv handling without `cli-utils`).
- No correctness change: cache keys, freshness and JSON bytes identical (parent AC4); full suite green.
- If the 60 MB target proves unreachable, the item records the measured floor with evidence and raises an OPEN QUESTION on the parent instead of silently relaxing the AC.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Re-run the F2 harness and profile the fast-path import graph.
2. Replace heavy imports still reachable from `read-cache-cli` (worklog-dir resolution, hashing, argv helpers) with minimal equivalents, deferring them to miss paths.
3. Tighten the F2 allowlist to the final set so the win cannot silently regress.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/worklog-paths.ts`
- `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`

## Dependencies

- F2 (harness and baseline)
- F4 (entry split)
- F6 (lazy registry, for the non-cache-hit command cost)
data.title: Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget

# F9 — Bound and prune the cache state directory via `wl doctor cache`

Implements desired change #4 and parent AC3: make the per-worklog-dir state counters a bounded, prunable on-disk store with a documented maintenance path, without touching freshness semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opportunistic pruning on cache writes keeps `state/` at or under a configured bound (default file count around 1,000 plus a TTL for untouched counters, aligned with the existing entry TTL/LRU). Measured on the reference host: a pre-populated 200k-file `state/` is reduced to the bound by one prune run, with file count, inode count and bytes quoted before and after in a comment.
- `wl doctor cache` exists with `--json`, a dry-run (report-only) mode and a prune mode. It reports file count, total bytes, stale-by-TTL count and live-dir count, and reclaims space when pruning. Bare `wl doctor` mentions pending cache state.
- Pruning is atomic and concurrency-safe (temp+rename, never truncating a live counter mid-write) and never deletes a counter whose worklog dir still has fresh cache entries; if entries exist, they are invalidated before the counter is dropped.
- Freshness correctness intact: the read-cache suites pass unchanged (parent AC4) and no stale read is served because a counter was pruned.
- The cap is configurable (env var or config key) with defaults safe on a Raspberry Pi class host, and the default is documented.
- Covers parent AC3: `~/.cache/wl/state/` is bounded and prunable — state storage is capped or consolidated, stale entries are removed, and a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it, with freshness semantics unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `pruneStateDir(cacheDir, { maxFiles, ttlMs, dryRun })` returning counts and bytes reclaimed.
2. Call it opportunistically and rate-limited (for example at most once per N minutes per process) from the cache write path, so growth is bounded without a daemon.
3. Add the `wl doctor cache` subcommand wiring the same function, reporting in text and `--json`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `CLI.md`
- `CONFIG.md`

## Dependencies

- F8 (tests first).
data.title: Bound and prune cache state via wl doctor cache

# F10 — Verify the >= 60 % CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle

Parent AC2's measurement and decision point. With F1 instrumentation, measure total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on one shared worklog dir, before and after the fast path, and only then decide whether herdr read coalescing is additionally required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A repeatable measurement procedure is recorded (env `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, 4 panes running the herdr query set over one 30 s cycle, warm cache) with the exact command quoted in a comment.
- Baseline and after numbers are both quoted in comments on this item and on the parent: total CPU-seconds, spawn count, cache-hit count, p95 per-spawn wall time and RSS.
- After <= 0.4x baseline total CPU-seconds (>= 60 % reduction) is demonstrated, or the shortfall is quantified with the dominant remaining cost identified.
- If the target is missed, the item records which lever is needed. Given herdr already has in-flight memoisation and in-process SQLite reads (`WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG`, `WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B`), it either (a) implements a bounded, stateless coalescing refinement in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (one consolidated read per refresh tick) or (b) files a `discovered-from` child when the change exceeds this item's scope.
- No correctness regression: herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state and the spawn-reduction simulation test still passes.
- Covers parent AC2: total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on a shared worklog dir drops >= 60 % versus current behaviour, measured by the env-gated spawn instrumentation with per-process CPU time; baseline and after numbers quoted.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Build a 4-pane measurement harness reusing the patterns in `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` plus F1 aggregation.
2. Measure the pre-split build first (worktree of `dev`, or `WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1` for the read-work baseline), then re-measure after F4 to F7.
3. Record numbers and the lever decision in comments.

**Key Files:**
- `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (CPU and RSS instrumentation)
- F6 (lazy per-command imports)
- F7 (fast-path budget)

# Canonical test suite excludes 76 root-level tests/*.test.ts files

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the canonical suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. Vitest therefore runs tests/cli (104 files) and tests/unit (43 files) only: the 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files (`tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`, `tests/audit.test.ts`, …) are never executed by /skill:test, implement.py finish, the pre-push hook, the ship release gate or an audit F3 auto-run.

## Goal

The canonical full suite executes every test file, or each exclusion is documented with a rationale.

## Users / Stakeholders

- **Agent tiers** (implement, audit, test): rely on the canonical full suite for gate enforcement.
- **Producer**: needs the canonical suite to be a reliable proxy for repo health.
- **CI**: uses `npm test` (full vitest suite, 370+ files) — the canonical subset is not a reliable proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical suite command(s) in `.pi/test-config.json` cover root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files, or each exclusion is documented with a reason.
- A full /skill:test run reports the root-level files as executed (currently 0 of 76).
- Root-level failures surfaced by the change are triaged into test-failure items.
- Documented in docs/dev/ (test-suite layout) so work items cannot claim coverage the gate does not provide.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Runtime budget:** The existing canonical suite takes ~305s (tests/cli + tests/unit). The 76 root-level files add an unknown but potentially significant cost. Must be measured before/after.
- **Vitest configuration:** `vitest.config.ts` uses default glob patterns that discover all test files — the current suiteCommands narrow this to only `tests/cli` and `tests/unit`. Root-level files must be added without breaking the singleFork/isolation setup.
- **Overlapping basenames:** 4 files (`audit.test.ts`, `doctor-foreign-items-apply.test.ts`, `process-lifecycle.test.ts`, `sync-author-gate.test.ts`) exist at both root and in `tests/cli/` — these may be duplicates, relocations, or intentional variants. The change must not cause double-execution.
- **Related sibling:** WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (canonical full suite excludes herdr package tests — completed) addresses the same root cause for a different scope; coordinate to avoid conflicting changes to `.pi/test-config.json`.

## Existing State

- `.pi/test-config.json`: declares `suiteCommands` as `tests/cli` + `tests/unit` (104 + 43 = 147 files)
- `vitest.config.ts`: discovers 370+ test files via default globs, but gates narrow to canonical subset
- 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files never executed by any gate
- 4 files have both root and `tests/cli/` variants
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` documents canonical suite coverage but not the exclusion rationale

## Desired Change

Add the root-level test files to the canonical suite in `.pi/test-config.json` (either by expanding `suiteCommands` or introducing a named `groups` section — the test skill supports `groups` in the config), or document each exclusion with a rationale. Measure runtime impact. Update `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (or create `docs/dev/test-suite-layout.md`) with coverage documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add root-level test path to suiteCommands or groups
- `vitest.config.ts` — verify no conflicts with new glob patterns
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update with new coverage numbers
- `tests/*.test.ts` — the 76 files to be covered (or documented as excluded)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **4 overlapping files** risk double execution if globs add both `tests/*.test.ts` and `tests/cli/*.test.ts`/`tests/unit/*.test.ts` variants (audit, doctor-foreign-items-apply, process-lifecycle, sync-author-gate). Must deduplicate (either via vitest default globs or explicit path sets) and verify executed-file count vs expected.
- **Runtime growth unknown** — root files are never run today; full-suite budget may grow beyond the existing ~305 s. Measure before/after; if any single file is pathologically slow, document (exclusion rationale) rather than silently exclude.
- **Hidden failures** — the 76 files may already be red; surfacing them will create test-failure triage work (AC3 explicitly requires this; the change must NOT be blocked by triage, but failures must not be left un-triaged).
- **Sibling fix may not have landed** — WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (herdr) reports completed, but `.pi/test-config.json` currently has no herdr coverage and only 2 commits ever touched the file. Verify whether its fix landed elsewhere or was reverted; do not assume `.pi/test-config.json` already reflects completed sibling work.
- **Assumption:** the canonical suite intent is full-suite parity with `npm test` (CI) — exclusions only acceptable with documented rationale (per Goal).

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — Canonical full suite excludes herdr package tests (same root cause, different scope; completed — its solution pattern for extending `.pi/test-config.json` should be reused/checked for conflicts)

# Model in use does not update in Pi plugin

## Headline

The Worklog Pi extension footer (Line 3, right-aligned) shows a stale "model in use" after a mid-session model switch: the newly selected alias is paired with the previous session's resolved provider/model until the next Local Proxy response arrives — and permanently so when the switched-to model is not proxy-routed (e.g. a direct `deepseek` or `opencode` provider), because the `X-Resolved-Model` header never arrives. Intake RCA: `_resolvedModel` is never invalidated on `model_select` (only on `session_start`).

## Problem statement

After `/model` (or model cycling) mid-session, the footer's resolved provider/model does not update properly — it keeps showing the previously resolved model instead of the newly selected one. Root cause (confirmed by code reading): in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts`, the resolved value (`_resolvedModel`) is only ever (a) set from the Local Proxy `X-Resolved-Model` response header in `after_provider_response`, or (b) reset to `null` on `session_start` (see WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6). The `model_select` handler updates only `_selectedModel`. Two observable outcomes:

1. Immediately after a switch, the footer shows `newAlias → oldResolvedModel` (stale/misleading) until the first response carrying a new header arrives.
2. If the switched-to model is served by a non-proxy provider (`deepseek`, `opencode` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`) no `X-Resolved-Model` header ever arrives, so the stale value persists for the rest of the session — or, if we only cleared the cache, the footer would show `(resolving)` forever, which is equally wrong.

## Users

- **Pi operator** switching models mid-session (e.g. `code` → `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) to control cost/latency: needs the footer to reflect the switch immediately so they trust which model is actually serving the session.
  - *User story:* "When I run `/model` to switch to a cheaper or local model, I expect the footer to show the new model right away — not the old one — and definitely not forever."
- **Producer/auditor** reviewing recorded sessions: the displayed model must be trustworthy for RCA and cost attribution.
  - *User story:* "I check the footer to confirm which model handled a turn; a stale label makes the record unreliable."

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `model_select` fires mid-session (sources `set` and `cycle`), the previously resolved model is immediately invalidated: `getResolvedModel()` returns `null` right after the handler runs and the footer shows `<newAlias> → (resolving)` until a fresh proxy response arrives. Unit-testable in `model-display.test.ts` and a footer-render regression test in `session-health.test.ts`.
- When the selected model's provider is not the Local Proxy (no `X-Resolved-Model` header can arrive), the footer displays the model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of a stale proxy value or an unbounded `(resolving)` state. The proxy provider is identified by name (`Local Proxy`) — the same convention already centralised in `@worklog/shared/lease-release` (`LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME`).
- Subsequent proxy responses update the resolved value exactly as today (header extraction, uppercase/lowercase handling, no-op on identical values, `onModelChange` firing) — no regression to existing behaviour covered by `model-display.test.ts`.
- The fix is fail-open when config is unavailable/unknown (no throw, no crash); existing `(resolving)`, right-alignment, and width-handling behaviour on Footer Line 3 (WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P, WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP, WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5) is preserved.
- At least one unit test covers the end-to-end footer rendering for a mid-session switch (new alias + invalidation) and for the non-proxy provider case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (`packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — "Model/Provider Display (Line 3)" state table and the `model_select` event-row meaning), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Changes are confined to the Worklog Pi extension package (`packages/tui/extensions`); no local-proxy changes (the proxy already emits `x-resolved-model` on every response it routes — verified by the earlier spike SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 and a live probe).
- Must preserve the intermediate `(resolving)` state introduced by WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P and the session-start reset fix (WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6) — this work is the mid-session analogue of that fix.
- Non-TUI modes must keep degrading gracefully (footer is a no-op outside TUI).
- Keep the fix surgical: no speculative refactor of the model-display module.

## Existing state

- `model-display.ts` (6222 B): module-level `_resolvedModel` / `_selectedModel`; `_onModelChange` is a **single callback slot** (multi-subscriber clobbering is a latent defect but not currently triggered). Listeners: `session_start` (resets `_resolvedModel`, seeds `_selectedModel` if unset), `model_select` (sets `_selectedModel` only), `after_provider_response` (sets `_resolvedModel` from `x-resolved-model`/`X-Resolved-Model` header only when it differs).
- `session-health.ts` (Line 3 render): `${selectedModel} → ${resolvedModel}`, else `alias → (resolving)`, else `resolvedModel`, else `—`. Subscribes via `onModelChange(() => tui.requestRender())` on first render.
- Pi SDK: `model_select` event carries `{ model: {provider, id}, previousModel, source: "set"|"cycle"|"restore" }` and fires on `/model`, model cycling, and session restore (verified in `pi-coding-agent` types `ModelSelectEvent` and `examples/extensions/model-status.ts`). `after_provider_response` exposes the raw HTTP response headers (lowercase-normalised).
- Proxy provider config lives in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; the project already centralises the `Local Proxy` provider-name constant and models.json lookup in `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts`.

## Desired change

1. In the `model_select` handler of `model-display.ts`: invalidate `_resolvedModel` (set `null`) and notify `_onModelChange` so the footer re-renders to `newAlias → (resolving)`.
2. If the newly selected model's provider is not the configured Local Proxy provider, treat the model's own `provider/id` as the resolved value immediately (no `(resolving)` limbo), so the footer shows the true model.
3. No change to the render logic in `session-health.ts` is expected (it already handles `null` resolved); add only regression tests. If a change becomes necessary it must keep the existing right-align and width-budget behaviour.
4. Update `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` to document the mid-session invalidation and the non-proxy fallback in the state table.

## Key Files:

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` — invalidate `_resolvedModel` on `model_select`; derive `provider/id` fallback for non-proxy providers.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.test.ts` — new tests: mid-session switch invalidation (all sources), non-proxy fallback, no regression to header extraction.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — footer Line 3 render regression test for mid-session switch and non-proxy provider.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — verify only (render already null-aware); touch only if tests reveal otherwise.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document updated `model_select` semantics and new fallback display.
- (reference, not changed) `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` — canonical `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` convention to reuse.

## Related work

- WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 (completed) — Reset resolved model on session_start to avoid stale display across sessions. **Direct sibling:** same stale-display class; fixed at session boundary only, leaving the mid-session hole this item covers.
- WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P (completed) — Show model status in pi quickly; introduced the `(resolving)` intermediate state.
- WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0 / WL-0MRF19R71004YJND (completed) — Session Health footer and the Line-3 model/provider line.
- WL-0MRC3F30E008XJN3 / WL-0MRC91VIN0089UXD / WL-0MRC3NOVZ000P0P5 (completed) — Model-display extension integration into the Worklog extension (status-line provenance).
- WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP, WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 (completed) — Line-3 right-alignment/truncation and alias/command position swaps that must not regress.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risks**
  - Header-based resolution remains the single source of truth for proxy-routed models; if a switch does not produce a new header (identical downstream model, request failure, non-proxy fallback routes), the footer can still lag. Mitigation: AC2 shows the selected model's own `provider/id` for non-proxy providers; `(resolving)` is the honest state while a proxy response is pending.
  - Some providers in `models.json` run under `modelOverrides` (e.g. `opencode`); deriving `${provider}/${id}` must use the *selected* model's provider/id, not overrides, to stay truthful.
  - Scope-creep risk: do not also "fix" the single-slot `onModelChange` (latent, no current trigger) or alias staleness on `session_start` guard (`! _selectedModel`) in this item — record as `discovered-from` follow-ups instead if the implementer confirms they are real.
- **Assumptions (documented, communicated on completion)**
  - A1. The observed defect is the stale resolved model after a mid-session switch, in both proxy and non-proxy scenarios (the only code path consistent with "does not update properly").
  - A2. The proxy provider is identified by the literal name `Local Proxy` (project convention in `lease-release.ts`); no config re-read is required if the check is by provider name against the constant, otherwise reuse the shared models.json lookup.
  - A3. On any mid-session `model_select` (including `restore`), invalidating the resolved value is correct; `session_start` already resets at session boundaries.
- **Open confirmation questions for the producer (non-blocking — see Appendix)**

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What exactly did you observe when changing the model mid-session — did the left-hand alias update while the right-hand resolved model stayed on the previous one (or until the next turn), or did the whole label fail to change?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded for producer confirmation). Research: the code only updates the resolved half from the `X-Resolved-Model` response header and invalidates it only on `session_start`, so the stale-resolved/lagging scenarios are the only code-consistent outcomes. Assumption A1 covers both.
- Q2: "When the switched-to model is NOT served by the Local Proxy (e.g. direct `deepseek`/`opencode` providers in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`), should the footer show the selected model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of an endless `(resolving)`?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — Recommended: yes** (shows the true serving model; `(resolving)` forever is untruthful). Assumption A2.
- Q3: "Should invalidating the resolved value also apply when the model is restored/re-selected at session start (`source: restore`), consistent with the WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 session-start reset?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — Recommended: yes** (uniform behaviour; `session_start` already resets). Assumption A3.

  Research summary: pi's `model_select` events carry `model.provider`/`model.id` and `source` (`set|cycle|restore`); `after_provider_response` carries the raw HTTP headers and the Local Proxy adds `x-resolved-model` on the responses it routes (live-verified in spike SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0). No new pi-version of the SDK contract is required.

Automated repo-file matches were reviewed and discarded as keyword noise (the full untruncated report is retained at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB.md`). The high-signal related files are listed under **Key Files** above.

## Goal

Make the Worklog extension footer show the model that is **actually** serving the session immediately after a mid-session model switch — invalidating the stale resolved value and falling back to the selected model's own `provider/id` when no proxy header can ever arrive.

## Context

Parent: `WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB`. Today `model_select` updates only `_selectedModel`, so the footer pairs the new alias with the previous resolved model; for non-proxy providers (`deepseek`, `opencode`, `opencode-go` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`) the `x-resolved-model` header never arrives and the stale value persists for the rest of the session.

## Implementation (surgical — no speculative refactor)

1. **Invalidate on selection** — in the `model_select` handler of `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts`, clear `_resolvedModel` to `null` for every source (`set` / `cycle` / `restore`) and notify `_onModelChange` exactly once so the footer re-renders to `<newAlias> → (resolving)`.
2. **Non-proxy fallback** — when the selected model's `provider` is not the Local Proxy, set `_resolvedModel` to `${model.provider}/${model.id}` (the *selected* model's provider/id — never `modelOverrides`) instead of leaving it `null`.
3. **Proxy-provider selections** — when the provider **is** the Local Proxy, leave `_resolvedModel` as `null` so the honest `(resolving)` state shows until a real `x-resolved-model` header arrives.
4. **Shared provider-name constant** — reuse the canonical `Local Proxy` name. The constant currently exists as a **private** `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` in `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` and is **not exported**. Recommended: add the `export` keyword there (a one-line, non-behavioural change; `packages/shared` is not the local proxy and the extension already imports `@worklog/shared/lease-release`). If the producer prefers to honour the "changes confined to `packages/tui/extensions`" constraint literally, define a local constant in `model-display.ts` that cites the shared convention in a comment. Record whichever option is taken in a comment on this item.
5. **Fail-open** — a missing/unknown provider, missing model, or unreadable config must not throw; degrade to `null` (→ `(resolving)`) exactly as today. No new I/O on the render path.
6. **No render changes expected** — `session-health.ts` already handles a `null` resolved value; touch it only if the new tests prove otherwise, and then preserve right-alignment and the width budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `model_select` with `source: "set"`, `"cycle"` or `"restore"` leaves `getResolvedModel() === null` and `getSelectedModel()` set to the new id, and fires `onModelChange` once.
- When the selected model's provider is not the Local Proxy (no `X-Resolved-Model` header can arrive), the footer displays the model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of a stale value or an unbounded `(resolving)` state — the provider is identified by name (`Local Proxy`, the `@worklog/shared/lease-release` convention).
- Selecting a Local Proxy model keeps `getResolvedModel() === null` until an `x-resolved-model` header arrives; subsequent proxy responses update the resolved value exactly as today (header extraction, uppercase/lowercase handling, no-op on identical values, `onModelChange` firing) — no regression to behaviour covered by `model-display.test.ts` (parent AC3).
- A missing model, missing provider, or unavailable/unknown config does not throw and degrades to `null` (fail-open, no crash) — covered by tests.
- The provider-name check reuses the canonical `Local Proxy` constant (exported from `@worklog/shared/lease-release`, or a documented local equivalent) — no duplicated magic strings without a comment.
- All tests added by the sibling test item pass, and no pre-existing test in `model-display.test.ts` or `session-health.test.ts` regresses.
- The fix is fail-open when config is unavailable/unknown (no throw, no crash); `session-health.ts` is unchanged unless a test proves a render change is required, and any such change preserves the existing `(resolving)`, right-alignment and width-handling behaviour on Footer Line 3 (parent AC4).

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` — the only expected production change (handler + fallback helper).
- `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` — optional one-line `export` of `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` (decision recorded in a comment).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — verify only; do not change speculatively.

## Notes

- Depends on the test item — do not start until those tests exist and are red.
- Prerequisite test item: "Tests: mid-session model-switch invalidation and non-proxy fallback".
- Keep the single-slot `onModelChange` and the `session_start` `!_selectedModel` guard untouched (latent, out of scope — see parent Risks).
- Run tests only via the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope).

# Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
- Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
- **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The bundle must be a pure read to be deterministically cacheable, so it uses `--no-re-sort`-style selection and the re-sort is treated as a separate concern; output parity is guarded by a test. Recorded as a risk above. Source: `src/commands/next.ts` auto re-sort logic.
- **Q:** Is a fail-open fallback required?
  **A (agent, derived from existing fetcher design):** Yes — the fetcher's existing in-process fast paths all fail open to `wl` spawns; the consolidated read follows the same convention. Source: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`.
