# Herdr downtime dispatch: use the proxy's local_idle_seconds as the idle-age signal

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy now publishes an authoritative local idle age
(`local_idle_seconds`, plus `local_last_activity_at` and
`local_last_activity_source`), but herdr measures idle duration itself from
its own polls. If the GPU has already been idle for hours when herdr starts
polling (plugin restart, pane restart, resumed session), herdr still waits a
full `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` before dispatching; conversely its sampled
tracker can be fooled by gaps in polling. Both outcomes leave the local model
idle when it could be working.

## Users

- **Operator / producer:** wants downtime dispatch to start as soon as the
  local GPU has genuinely been idle long enough, including immediately after
  a herdr restart.
- **Downtime dispatcher (herdr plugin):** wants the proxy's authoritative
  idle age instead of inferring it from poll cadence.

Example stories:

- As the operator, after restarting herdr while the GPU has been idle for two
  hours, I want the next downtime pane dispatched on the first poll rather
  than after another threshold wait.
- As the dispatcher, when the proxy reports `local_idle_seconds` below the
  threshold, I should not dispatch even if my local tracker has an older idle
  run (the proxy is authoritative).

## Evidence / existing state (llm-manager)

Upstream capability is **already implemented and deployed** on llm-manager
`dev` (commit `05986c1b`, `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`). `GET /llama/local/status`
now serves:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `local_idle_seconds` | `float \| null` | Monotonic idle age of the local backend; updated on dispatch start, on every forwarded SSE chunk, and on request finish. Baseline is proxy process start, so a freshly restarted proxy reports its true idle age rather than "unknown". |
| `local_last_activity_at` | ISO string \| null | Wall-clock timestamp of the last local activity (operator-facing). |
| `local_last_activity_source` | string \| null | What last touched the backend (`dispatch` / `chunk` / `finish` / startup …). |

The same upstream change also added idle-aware local admission on the proxy
(`local_idle_admit_enabled`, default off), which reads exactly this signal.

Relevant existing herdr behaviour (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`):

- `createIdleTracker()` records idle runs from the worker's own poll results;
  `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` is the continuous-idle threshold.
- Per-slot mode tracks the same N slots continuously free
  (`perSlotTracker.thresholdMetCount`).
- `globalIdleChecks()` requires `local_active_query === false` (all-slots-free
  mode); the spare-capacity path relaxes it.
- `LlamaStatus` does **not** parse `local_idle_seconds`.

Contract source: llm-manager `proxy/docs/routing.md` § "Idle-aware local
admission" (idle signal description) and
`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`.

## Desired change

1. Extend `LlamaStatus` / `parseLlamaStatus` with `local_idle_seconds`,
   `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source` (all optional;
   malformed values degrade to `undefined`, never throw).
2. When `local_idle_seconds` is present and finite, use it as the
   **authoritative** idle-age signal for threshold qualification:
   - `idle_seconds >= thresholdSeconds` → the idle threshold is already met
     on this poll (no need to wait for the local tracker to accumulate).
   - `idle_seconds < thresholdSeconds` → not yet qualified; do **not** admit
     on the strength of an older local tracker run (the proxy is
     authoritative).
   - absent / non-finite → fall back to today's local tracker behaviour
     exactly (pre-feature proxy).
3. Keep the immediate busy reset: a poll that shows activity
   (`is_processing`, a live lease, any contention/gate waiter) still resets
   the idle run regardless of the reported idle age.
4. Use `local_last_activity_source` in the decision log (and optionally the
   header) to explain *why* the backend is considered busy/idle (e.g.
   `chunk`, `dispatch`, `finish`) — this is operator-facing evidence, not a
   gate.
5. Do not weaken the per-slot contract: `local_idle_seconds` is a global
   signal; it may only *satisfy* the per-slot continuous-free requirement
   when the same poll also provides usable per-slot detail and no slot is
   processing/owned. If per-slot detail is absent/empty/stale, the existing
   `slots-unavailable` fail-closed path still applies.
6. Preserve `requiredFreeSlots` semantics: the idle-age signal qualifies the
   *duration*, not the *capacity*; the free-slot budget is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `parseLlamaStatus` reads `local_idle_seconds`,
  `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source`; absent fields
  preserve today's behaviour, and malformed values degrade to `undefined`
  without throwing (tests).
- [ ] With `local_idle_seconds >= thresholdSeconds` reported on the first
  poll (fresh worker, usable per-slot detail, no activity), the worker
  dispatches without waiting for the local tracker to accumulate the
  threshold (test).
- [ ] With `local_idle_seconds < thresholdSeconds`, the worker does **not**
  dispatch even when its local tracker already has an older idle run (test).
- [ ] A poll reporting activity (per-slot `is_processing`, live lease, or a
  contention/gate waiter) resets the idle run regardless of a large
  `local_idle_seconds` (test).
- [ ] `local_idle_seconds` absent (pre-feature proxy) restores exactly
  today's local-tracker behaviour (regression test).
- [ ] `slots_stale: true`, `slots: []` or unusable per-slot detail still
  yields `slots-unavailable` even when `local_idle_seconds` is large (test —
  the global signal must not bypass the per-slot fail-closed contract).
- [ ] The decision log records `local_idle_seconds` (and
  `local_last_activity_source` when present) so an operator can see why a
  dispatch was admitted or deferred (test asserts the logged fields).
- [ ] Tests are written red-first and cover every transition above using the
  existing fixtures (`downtime-worker.parse.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.idle.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (idle detection description and
  `downtimeIdleThresholdMs`) and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (idle-age
  authority and fallback behaviour).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatible:** absent idle fields must behave exactly as today.
- **Fail closed on ambiguity:** a non-finite/malformed idle age is ignored
  (fallback to the local tracker), never treated as "idle forever".
- **Global signal, local contract:** `local_idle_seconds` never bypasses the
  per-slot availability/fail-closed rules.
- **No new polling:** reuse the existing single-flight status poll.
- Keep the change surgical: prefill/concurrency pacing is the sibling item
  `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`; per-slot `lease_state`/`capacity_hint` availability
  is `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `LlamaStatus`,
  `parseLlamaStatus`, `createIdleTracker` / tick idle qualification,
  per-slot tick path, decision-log builder, `decisionHeaderToken` if a new
  reason is introduced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` — new fields,
  malformed/absent cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.test.ts` — threshold
  qualification, busy reset, stale/unusable interplay.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — end-to-end tick and
  decision-log assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — idle-signal fixtures.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — idle detection contract and threshold.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — idle-age authority.

## Related work

**Upstream (llm-manager)**

- `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` — Idle-aware local admission for large/cold prompts —
  completed (`05986c1b`); publishes `local_idle_seconds` and the activity
  source.
- `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` — truthful capacity payload (`capacity_hint`,
  `lease_state`); the availability sibling.
- `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ` — prefill serialisation; the pacing sibling.
- `LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1` — stale log-derived slot-progress expiry; keeps the
  per-slot `n_decoded` signal honest (a related proxy-side fix).

**ContextHub**

- `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` — **blocks this item**: truthful per-slot capacity
  parsing/gating.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` — sibling: prefill-serialisation pacing.
- `WL-0MSP28LSY007NDYX` / `WL-0MT3D585I0070FF0` — per-slot idle tracking and
  the relaxed idle gate (the behaviour this item qualifies).
- `WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q` — `local_active_query` as the local busy signal
  (precedent for preferring a proxy-authoritative signal).
- `WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW` — fail-closed per-slot contract.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk — clock/baseline semantics:** `local_idle_seconds` is monotonic and
  proxy-process-relative; a proxy restart resets it to a small value even if
  the GPU was idle before. The local tracker remains a valid fallback, so the
  worker may still wait a threshold after a proxy restart — acceptable and
  documented.
- **Risk — bypassing per-slot continuous-free semantics:** mitigated by
  keeping the per-slot fail-closed preconditions and only using the global
  age as a *duration* qualification.
- **Assumption** — `local_idle_seconds` reflects all local activity
  (dispatch start, chunks, finish), so "idle ≥ threshold" implies every slot
  has been idle that long.
- **Assumption** — `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` remains the user-facing
  threshold; no new setting is needed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not expand into proxy admission changes
  (`local_idle_admit_enabled`) — that is upstream and off by default.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the upstream implementation and its
published contract fully determine this brief. Evidence reviewed:

- llm-manager `dev` commit `05986c1b`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`
  § "Idle-aware local admission", `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py`.
- llm-manager `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` description and acceptance criteria.
- llm-manager `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` `get_llama_local_status()` idle
  fields.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`createIdleTracker`,
  `evaluateIdle`, per-slot tick), `packages/herdr/README.md`,
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Worklog searches: `local_idle_seconds`, `idle`, `slot` — no existing
  ContextHub idle-age consumer item found (duplicate check performed).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** – Herdr downtime dispatch: consume truthful per-slot capacity (lease_state / capacity_hint / prefill ETA) (in-progress)
- **WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX** – Herdr downtime dispatch: pace dispatch to local prefill serialisation (blocked)
- **WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7** – Raise default downtime idle threshold to 75s so active sessions reclaim freed slots before dispatch (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0muxvpxaz005resw, absent, acceptable, acceptance, active (+298 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0muxvpxaz005resw, absent, accumulate, active, activity (+285 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, active, activity, added, age (+225 more)

## Goal

As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want the performance harnesses and shared test fixtures ready to measure and verify a single consolidated `wl` read, so that the spawn-reduction target (parent AC3) is measurable before the consolidated command exists and every later slice can be tested without re-inventing fixtures.

This is the test-first slice of parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS: it adds measurement/verification infrastructure only and changes no production behaviour.

## Scope

- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` currently hard-code the five-query legacy set (`QUERIES`). Add a query-set selector (`--query-set legacy|consolidated`, default `legacy`) so the same harness measures one consolidated invocation per refresh tick while keeping the historical numbers comparable. In C1 the `consolidated` path is plumbing only: it must degrade cleanly (a clear "invocation not available yet" report/no-op, non-zero exit only when explicitly requested) because `wl worklist` does not exist until WL-C2.
- Add a reusable seeded-worklog fixture helper for the new CLI and herdr tests: root and child items spanning critical / in_review (completed + in-progress) / blocked / in-progress / open non-critical, at least one with a stored audit result, and at least one child under a root so `--root-only` filters are provably exercised.
- Extend `tests/bench/herdr-refresh-perf.test.ts` (or add a focused sibling) to cover the query-set selector plumbing and the consolidated-vs-legacy baseline ratio computation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` accepts `--query-set legacy` (default) and `--query-set consolidated`, issues exactly one invocation per tick in `consolidated` mode, and reports spawn counts / CPU-seconds for whichever set is selected.
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` accepts the same selector and reports spawn count and latency for the selected set.
- An invalid `--query-set` value exits non-zero with an explicit error naming the valid values.
- The `consolidated` set is defined from a single exported constant so the CLI invocation vector lives in one place (no duplicated argv in bench and tests).
- A shared seeded-worklog fixture helper exists and is reused by at least one test, seeding the subset mix above (verified by assertions on the seeded data: ≥1 critical, ≥1 completed/in_review, ≥1 in-progress/in_review, ≥1 blocked root, ≥1 open non-critical, ≥1 child item).
- The reduction ratio is computed from a measured legacy baseline, not a hard-coded constant, and a test asserts the ratio arithmetic (e.g. 5 → 1 spawn yields 80 % reduction).
- No production source file (`src/`, `packages/herdr/src/` excluding tests) changes behaviour in this slice.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC3: measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10), total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to ≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s), ideally ~5× fewer spawns; this slice supplies the measurement harness for that comparison.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC8: the full project test suite must pass with the new changes; this slice keeps the suite green and documents its target.

## Minimal implementation

1. Export `LEGACY_WORKLIST_QUERIES` and `CONSOLIDATED_WORKLIST_QUERY` (single `worklist` argv) from one shared location importable by bench and tests.
2. Add `--query-set` parsing to both harnesses with validation and default `legacy`.
3. Route the tick loop through the selected set; in `consolidated` mode collect a clear "unavailable" diagnostic instead of a hard crash when the command is absent.
4. Factor the CPU/spawn summary maths into a helper that takes baseline and candidate measurements.
5. Add the seeded-worklog fixture helper next to the existing `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` helpers.
6. Add/extend bench tests for the selector and ratio arithmetic; update each harness's header doc comment.

## Key Files

- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — add `--query-set` selector, single-invocation consolidated tick
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` — add `--query-set` selector and consolidated reporting
- `tests/bench/herdr-refresh-perf.test.ts` — selector + ratio arithmetic coverage
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded-worklog fixture helper
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — consumes the shared query-set constants (no new assertions yet)

## Dependencies

- None (first slice).

## Deliverables

- Harness selector + shared query-set constants.
- Seeded-worklog fixture helper.
- Bench plumbing tests.
- Updated harness doc comments explaining the two query sets and the target ratio.

## Notes

- Keep the default `legacy` set byte-identical to today's five queries so F10's recorded numbers (159.44 → 83.58 CPU-s/cycle) remain comparable.

## Goal

As a wl CLI maintainer, I want a dedicated `wl worklist --json` read command that returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload from **one DB open**, built from the same query and selection code the individual commands use, so that Herdr can issue one read per refresh tick instead of five.

## Scope

Parent AC1 (command half). This slice delivers the command plus its tests; caching is WL-C3 and the fetcher consumer is WL-C4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl worklist --json` exists and is registered as a built-in command (present in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`, its lazy loader map, and the help metadata), with `--number/-n` (browse-feed count, default 20) and `--prefix` options.
- Its JSON payload contains five named subsets — `critical`, `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots`, `browse` — plus payload metadata (at minimum the resolved worklog dir and the browse count requested). Each subset key is **always present**, as an empty array rather than omitted, when it has no members.
- The four list subsets use exactly the existing filters: critical = `--priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (all parent levels); review queue = `--status completed,in-progress --stage in_review --root-only`; in-progress roots = `--status in-progress --root-only`; blocked roots = `--status blocked --root-only`.
- The `browse` subset matches `wl next -n <count> --include-in-progress --include-blocked --no-re-sort --json` item-for-item and order-for-order for the same DB state, including the audit (`auditResult`, `auditedAt`), `childCount` and group (`group`, `groupLabel`) enrichment that `wl next` emits.
- The command opens the database **exactly once** per invocation (asserted by a spy/counter test) and issues all five reads against that single handle.
- The command is a **pure read**: it never calls `reSort` and never bumps the read-cache state counter (asserted by comparing the counter file before/after).
- The browse feed is bounded by the requested count; mandatory subsets are returned unfiltered by that count.
- `--worklog-dir` (global option) works unchanged, and no item appears in `browse` that would not appear in `wl next` for the same arguments.
- Duplication is avoided by extracting the browse-feed selection + enrichment currently inline in `src/commands/next.ts` into a shared helper called by **both** `next` and `worklist` (no forked selection logic).
- New tests cover: payload shape with an empty DB, payload shape with the seeded fixture, per-subset filter parity against the equivalent `wl list` invocation, browse-feed parity against `wl next --no-re-sort`, single DB open, and pure-read behaviour.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC1: a single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command, sharing one DB open.

2. Add `src/commands/worklist.ts` registering `worklist`, resolving the DB once via `utils.getDatabase()`, running the four `db.list()` subset queries and the shared browse-feed selection, then emitting one `output.json()` payload.
3. Register the command in `src/command-registry.ts` and the help-group metadata in `src/cli-main.ts`.
4. Apply the `--no-re-sort` contract in code (never invoke `reSort`) and document it in the command description.

- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — **new** shared browse-feed selection/enrichment extracted from `next.ts`
- `src/commands/next.ts` — consume the extracted helper (behaviour unchanged)

## Goal

As a wl CLI maintainer, I want the new `wl worklist --json` invocation served from and backfilled into the existing on-disk read cache as a single cache entry, so repeat refreshes across Herdr panes hit the cache once per refresh instead of per subset.

## Scope

Parent AC1 (cache half) and AC4 (cache correctness).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `worklist` is added to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` and `isCacheableReadCommand('worklist')` returns true.
- A cacheable `wl worklist --json` invocation is served from cache on repeat with an unchanged DB: second invocation records a `cache-hit` spawn (`recordSpawn('cache-hit')`) and performs no DB work.
- A write (create/update/sync/comment…) bumps the state counter and invalidates the worklist entry; the next invocation does real read work and reflects the new DB state.
- The payload is keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` exactly like the other read commands — a different `--worklog-dir` or different `-n` count is a distinct entry.
- A mid-action write is not cached: when the state counter changes between lookup and `onJsonOutput`, the payload is not stored (same guard as today's commands).
- `WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1` disables both lookup and backfill for `worklist`.
- The cache serves the new command before the heavy command graph loads (the existing `src/cli.ts` preAction lookup path covers it; no new fast-path exception).
- New tests in `tests/cli/` cover: hit-on-repeat, invalidation-on-write, distinct keys for distinct `--worklog-dir`, and the disable env var.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC1: the consolidated `wl worklist --json` invocation is served as one read-cache entry.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC4: cache correctness unchanged — identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover read-cache hit and write-invalidation for the consolidated command.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `'worklist'` to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` in `src/read-cache-cli.ts`.
2. Verify — and adjust if needed — that `shouldCacheReadInvocation('worklist', argv)` returns true in JSON mode with no non-cacheable flags; `worklist` has no write-byproduct flags, so it should already be cacheable once listed.
3. Confirm the `src/cli.ts` / `src/cli-main.ts` lookup paths route the new command (no change expected; tests prove it).
4. Add `tests/cli/worklist-cache.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add `worklist` to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS`
- `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli-main.ts` — cache lookup wiring (verify unchanged)
- `tests/cli/worklist-cache.test.ts` — **new** hit/invalidation/keying/disable tests

- Cache hit/invalidation/keying/disable test coverage.

- The state-counter fingerprint and write-invalidation machinery are reused unchanged — do NOT fork the cache.

## Goal

As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want the default-view refresh to issue **one** `wl` read per tick — `wl worklist --json` — with the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root and blocked-root guarantees preserved and a fail-open fallback to today's per-subset spawn path when the consolidated read is unavailable.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (single read), AC5 (output parity), AC6 (fetcher tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fetchNextItems(count)` for a default-view refresh issues exactly **one** `runWl` invocation (`worklist`) when the command is available; no `wl list` or `wl next` spawns are issued for the bundle path (the in-flight fetch memo is bypassed for the bundle, or dedupes it, with no extra spawns).
- The mandatory subsets are derived from the bundle: all critical, all in_review (completed + in-progress), all in-progress roots and all blocked roots appear in the returned list regardless of the browse count (existing mandatory-guarantee tests still pass).
- `fetchReviewQueueState()` is derived from the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset (completed-only count + `auditsOutstanding`) and returns the same value as today's standalone `wl list` query for the same DB state.
- Audit enrichment is preserved: for items shared with mandatory `wl list` subsets, the richer `wl list`-style audit fields (`auditResult`, `auditedAt`, `fingerprint`, `currentFingerprint`) win over the `browse` representation, exactly as today (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G).
- Output parity: for the same DB state, the bundle path's final `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` output is identical to today's per-subset path (test compares both pipelines on the seeded fixture).
- Fail-open: when `wl worklist` is unavailable (older `wl`, non-zero exit, malformed/unparseable payload, missing subset key), the fetcher falls back to the existing per-subset spawns with byte-identical behaviour — the fallback path is asserted by a test that mocks the bundle failure.
- `wl next`'s auto re-sort is NOT triggered by the bundle (pure read); no write byproduct, so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- `--worklog-dir` and managed-worktree resolution behave unchanged (existing worktree tests still pass).
- New tests cover: single-spawn assertion, mandatory-subset presence, review-queue derivation, output parity, and fail-open fallback.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `worklist` to the fetcher's `MEMOIZABLE_COMMANDS` set (bundle is a cacheable read; memo dedupes identical concurrent refreshes — same as today).
2. Add `fetchWorklistBundle()` that runs `runWl(['worklist', '-n', String(count)])`, extracts the five subsets with `extractItems`, and validates the shape (unknown-shape ⇒ fail-open).
3. Rework `fetchNextItems(count)` to: try the bundle → derive mandatory sets + review-queue state + browse feed → merge/enrich with the existing `WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G` logic → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`; on any failure, fall back to today's `Promise.all([runWl(next), fetchMandatorySubsets()])` exactly.
4. Rework `fetchReviewQueueState()` to read the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset when already fetched in the same refresh, falling back to the standalone query.
5. Add `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` with injected fake `execFileAsync` covering the criteria.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchWorklistBundle`, reworked `fetchNextItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, memo set
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — **new** bundle tests
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-review-queue.test.ts`, `fetcher-include-blocked.test.ts`, `fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` — existing guarantees must keep passing
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded fixture (from WL-C1)

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C2 (`wl worklist` command + payload contract) and WL-C3 (cacheability).
- Depends on WL-C1 only transitively via WL-C2 (fixtures land in WL-C1; tests here reuse them).

## Deliverables

- Single-spawn default-view refresh with preserved mandatory guarantees.
- Review-queue state derived from the bundle.
- Fail-open fallback path.
- Fetcher test coverage including output parity.

## Notes

- Keep the browse feed bounded by the caller's count; mandatory subsets stay unfiltered by count.
- The re-sort write-byproduct risk (parent risk, medium) is handled by the command's `--no-re-sort`-style selection (WL-C2) plus this slice's output-parity test; if parity genuinely differs, record it as a comment and resolve separately rather than making the bundle a write.

## Goal

As a Herdr pane operator, I want `doRefresh` to run the whole default-view refresh from the single consolidated read — items, review-queue banner state and actionable context — so a refresh tick costs one `wl` process instead of five per pane.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (wire-through), AC5 (unchanged output), AC6 (worklist-level tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A default-view `doRefresh` cycle issues exactly **one** `wl` spawn for worklist data (asserted by a spawn-count integration test with an injected exec seam), down from five.
- The review-queue banner state (`applySprintState`) is populated from the same consolidated read — no separate review-queue spawn on the default view.
- Filtered views are unchanged: the stage-filtered (`fetchItemsByStage`), priority-filtered (`fetchItemsByPriority`) and recent-dispatches paths still use their existing reads, and the `activeDispatchFilter` path still merges live items from the default fetcher.
- Expanded-parent children still render correctly across the swap (no collapse flicker): the batched in-process children read continues to run concurrently with the consolidated item read, and the existing expand-across-refresh test passes.
- Idle behaviour is preserved: a refresh with no change still spawns zero `wl` processes where it did before (no new unconditional read).
- Event-loop responsiveness: the ≤ 100 ms p95 input-lag guard test still passes.
- Fail-open at the TUI layer: when the consolidated read fails, the refresh shows the per-subset fallback result (or the previous list) instead of an empty or errored view.
- New/extended tests cover the single-spawn default view, derived banner state, and unchanged filtered-view behaviour.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: the default-view refresh issues that single read per default-view refresh tick and the mandatory-subset guarantees are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state; existing fetcher tests and the spawn-reduction simulation pass.

## Fresh re-audit (post producer decisions) + runner-defect report

**Decisions applied:** AC1 targets updated to the measured floor (700 ms / 68 MB, `enforced: true`) in commit b4d5e0d2 (pushed to dev); AC2 accepted at the spawn-count gate; fresh re-audit run approved and executed (`--no-child-in-main-slot`, 9312 s, executed full-suite evidence at b4d5e0d2).

### Parent ACs on the fresh run — all clear
| AC | Verdict |
|---|---|
| AC1 import budget (700 ms / 68 MB, enforced) | **met** |
| AC2 >= 60 % CPU-second reduction | **adjusted** (variance: spawn-count gate accepted by producer, comment WL-C0MVHWM1WK008P7J2) |
| AC3 bounded/prunable cache state | **met** |
| AC4 no correctness regression | **met** |
| AC5 graceful degradation | **met** (previous run's misaligned 'unmet' did not reproduce) |
| AC6 tests + docs | **met** |

Merge gate: `b4d5e0d2` verified ancestor of `origin/dev`; stale-audit-base guard passed. Code quality: no findings. The AC5 reliability anomaly from the first run was a one-off artefact — this run verified it from the fallback code and fault-injection test.

### Why the persisted verdict is still 'No' — audit-runner defect (not a work gap)
The only blocker in the persisted report is:

> 11 children not yet in in_review/done stage: ... (all, plan_complete)

All 11 children were `completed`/`in_review` when this run started and were **stage-exempt**. During the run the runner's separate-process child-audit path **demoted every one of them**: F1 and F8 (the two dependency-free children) to `open`/`plan_complete`, and the other nine cascaded to `blocked`/`plan_complete` via the dependency chain — at the exact timestamp their child audits were persisted (11:58:45–48). This is the side-effect demotion forbidden by SA-0MUJAPC680078396 AC2 ('a parent-triggered re-screen must never silently push completed/in-review work back into the actionable queue or cascade blocked states through the dependency chain').

Aggravating factor: those child verdicts are infra-fallback-tainted — `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7` (7 child screens hit the 600 s child-screen budget). Per the skill's fallback rule an infra-fallback 'No' is not an explicit model assessment and must take the **restore** path, not the demotion path. Nine children were nonetheless demoted on those tainted verdicts (only F1/F2/F11 got 'Yes').

**Remediation applied:** all 11 children restored to their captured pre-audit state (`completed`/`in_review`, assignee cleared) in dependency order. Verified: 0 children outside completed/in_review. The stale in-main-slot pending-screens signal and checkpoint are gone.

**Verdict handling:** the runner's persisted 'No' is NOT overridden here (audit-skill rule) — it is reported as authoritative. With the children restored, its sole remaining blocker is the artefact above, so the parent is blocked on a tooling fix rather than on outstanding work.

### Recommended follow-ups (for the producer to file — the audit skill forbids creating items during an audit)
1. **bug (high):** separate-process child audits demote snapshot-exempt `in_review` children to `open`/`blocked` + `plan_complete`, cascading `blocked` through dependencies. Fix: extend the `_cascade_suppress_demotion` guarantee (currently keyed to the `AUDIT_CASCADE_AUDIT` marker) to parent-triggered child screens in both child-audit modes, and force the restore path on infra-fallback-tainted 'No' verdicts.
2. **chore (medium):** child Phase-1 screens time out at the 600 s `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT` budget on this host (7/27 calls), producing tainted verdicts; consider a larger child-screen budget or a smaller FILE SCOPE for child screens.
3. Once (1) is fixed, one more parent re-audit should return 'Ready to close: Yes' with no code changes needed.

## Implementation decisions (C1 verification harness)

**Shared query-set module** — new `bench/worklist-query-sets.ts` is the single home for the CLI invocation vectors:
- `LEGACY_WORKLIST_QUERIES` — the five F10 queries, kept byte-identical so the recorded 159.44 → 83.58 CPU-s/cycle numbers stay comparable.
- `CONSOLIDATED_WORKLIST_QUERY` — the single `['worklist','--json']` argv (no duplicated argv anywhere else; verified by grep).
- `parseWorklistQuerySet()` / `worklistQueriesFor()` — selector parsing and set lookup. Invalid or missing values throw with an explicit message naming `legacy, consolidated`.
- `computeReduction(baseline, candidate)` — spawn/CPU ratio maths derived from two measured runs (never hard-coded); zero baseline yields `null` ratio, not a divide-by-zero.

**Harnesses** — both accept `--query-set legacy|consolidated` (default `legacy`):
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts`: consolidated mode issues exactly one invocation per tick; report adds `querySet`, `queriesPerTick`, `spawnsPerRefresh`, `available`/`diagnostic`.
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts`: consolidated mode drives the single `wl worklist --json` read through the fetcher exec seam (so spawn accounting matches the legacy path); report adds `querySet`, `queriesPerRefresh`, `available`/`diagnostic`.
- C1 plumbing only: `wl worklist` does not exist until WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF, so an unavailable consolidated invocation is reported as a clear "not available yet" diagnostic and exits 0 — non-zero only when `--fail-if-unavailable` is passed explicitly.

**Pre-existing harness bug fixed** — `runTick` in the cycle harness resolved a local array it never filled, so `failures` was always 0 and `p95SpawnWallMs` always null. That would have hidden an unavailable consolidated invocation, so the results are now collected. Spawn/CPU totals are unaffected (they came from the spawn-record file).

**Seeded fixture** — `seedWorklistFixture(dir, opts)` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` writes config + init semaphore + item data (critical root, child under that root, completed/in_review, in-progress/in_review, blocked root, open non-critical, plus a stored audit result) and returns stable ids. Reused by `tests/cli/worklist-fixture.test.ts`, which asserts the mix through the real CLI (including `--root-only` excluding the child and the audit result being readable).

**Existing simulation** — `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` now consumes `LEGACY_WORKLIST_QUERIES` (no new assertions); run still reports 83.3% spawn reduction (30 → 5 work spawns, 5 cache hits).

**No production behaviour change**: no files under `src/` or `packages/herdr/src/` were touched.

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | A repeatable measurement procedure is recorded (env `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, 4 panes running the herdr query set over one 30 s cycle, warm cache) with the exact command quoted in a comment. | met | bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts:1-33 documents the procedure and quotes exact commands, with panes:4/cycleSeconds:30 (:61-62), WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE (:183) and a warm-cache cycle (:186-188). |

| 3 | After <= 0.4x baseline total CPU-seconds (>= 60 % reduction) is demonstrated, or the shortfall is quantified with the dominant remaining cost identified. | met | Item comment quantifies the 47.6% shortfall and names the dominant remaining cost (bare-node floor ~0.46 CPU-s, ~66% of what remains); harness reports cpuSeconds at bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts:246. |
| 4 | If the target is missed, the item records which lever is needed. Given herdr already has in-flight memoisation and in-process SQLite reads (`WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG`, `WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B`), it either (a) implements a bounded, stateless coalescing refinement in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (one consolidated read per refresh tick) or (b) files a `discovered-from` child when the change exceeds this item's scope. | adjusted | Lever recorded and follow-up WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS filed citing F10 evidence, but it is top-level (parentId null, no discovered-from link; only depends-on edges per wl dep) rather than a discovered-from child. |

| 6 | Covers parent AC2: total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on a shared worklog dir drops >= 60 % versus current behaviour, measured by the env-gated spawn instrumentation with per-process CPU time; baseline and after numbers quoted. | adjusted | CPU-seconds measured 159.44->83.58 (47.6%, above the 0.4x target) with numbers only on the child, but the producer accepted the spawn-count reduction gate as proxy evidence (parent comment WL-C0MVHWM1WK008P7J2). |
